name: VoiceManager__setParam
description: Voice manager parameter notify (vt 0x3c0701e8; a3 = k, a4 = value). Does not store the value. For k = 57 (PolyMode) it keeps round(value) as the mono flag byte +0x397 and, when it changes from 0 to non-zero, calls its own vtable slot +0x54 (all sound off). For k at most 82 it calls the layer object's virtual slot +0xc (this+4) and each of the 8 voices' virtual slot +0x20 (voice setParam 0x4037ac44) with k, unless those are the default stubs. The voices then read the new value themselves from the float block at voice+0x5b8 (manager word +8), at byte offset 4*k.

name: VoiceManager__noteOn
description: Part note-on (a2 = part, a3 = note, a4 = velocity, a5 passed on). Velocity 0 calls the note-off slot (vtable offset 24). Notes above 127 are ignored. Marks part+0x62c+note as 1 in the held table, stores the previous last note and sets the last note (s16 part+0x394) and last velocity (byte +0x396). Voice slots are 0x70 bytes at part+0x10, state byte slot+1 (0 free, 1 playing, 2 released, 3 fading), note s16 slot+2. Mono / legato mode (byte part+0x397 set): reuses the voice at index part+0x390; in state 1 or 2 Voice__start is called with glide flag 0, otherwise with flag 1. Poly mode: the busy count (slot 52 of the part vtable, default VoiceManager__busySlotCount) is compared with the polyphony limit (byte +0x392); the 8 voices are scanned starting after the round-robin index (+0x390). A free voice is used when the busy count is below the limit (Voice__start flag 1, round-robin index = that voice). Otherwise a victim is picked: the voice in state 2 with the oldest release stamp (slot+0x18/+0x1c); else, when the byte part+0x391 is set, the state 1 voice with the oldest trigger stamp (slot+0x10/+0x14), then the oldest state 3 voice; with +0x391 clear the voice with the highest note among those in states 1 and 3. The victim goes to state 3, its DSP voice gets Voice__fastFade (vtable offset 28), and the new note is parked as the pending note (slot+0x20 note, +0x22 previous note, +0x24 velocity, +0x26 release flag cleared, stamp copied to +0x10/+0x14) for VoiceManager__renderVoice to start when the fade finishes; the round-robin index becomes the victim. Read in full; VoiceManager__reset initializes the steal-selection high byte +0x391 to 1 via a 16-bit write of 0x0100 at +0x390 (the low byte +0x390 becomes 0); any later override of +0x391 has not been established. Round 105: The normal note-on allocation updates the round-robin slot index with s8i stores to manager+0x390 at 0x4037a615, 0x4037a6be, 0x4037a707, 0x4037a748 and 0x4037a78e. These do not touch manager+0x391, which reset sets to 1 with the overlapping s16i 0x0100. This does not prove no other indirect override exists.

name: VoiceManager__renderVoice
description: Per-block step of one voice slot (a2 = slot, a3/a4 = left/right output buffers, a5/a6 = 64-bit sample stamp). Returns 0 at once when the state byte slot+1 is 0. Otherwise runs three per-note value ramps (current values slot+48, +64, +80, targets from the tables at slot+96, +100, +104 indexed by the note, lengths s16 +62, +78, +94; each block the target is re-read, the step is recomputed as (target - current) / length and the current value moves one step, reaching the target when the counter hits 0; with a length below 1 no ramp runs), then renders the voice DSP object (slot+44 vtable offset 36) into the buffers. State handling: 2 (released): when Voice__isFinished (offset 24) the state becomes 0; 3 (fading): when finished, a pending note (s16 +32 not negative) is started with Voice__start (flag 1) and, if the byte +38 is set, the state becomes 2 and the DSP release (offset 20, byte +37) is called with the release stamp stored at +24/+28; otherwise the state becomes 0; state 1: age counter +8 += 16. Returns 1 for any slot that was not free at entry. Read in full.

name: VoiceManager__render
description: Per-block render of one part (a2 = part, a3/a4 = 16-float left/right outputs). Steps six parameter ramps (16 byte records at part+0x3cc + 0x10 k: current value, target at +4, step at +8, s16 counter at +12; when the counter reaches 0 the value takes the target), calls the tick slot (vtable offset 16, VoiceEngine__controlTick 0x4037e71c) of the shared DSP object at part+4, then renders the 8 voice slots (part+0x10 + 0x70 k) with VoiceManager__renderVoice into temporary buffers; the first active voice's output is copied, later ones are added (four floats at a time); with no active voice both outputs are zeroed. Finally the 64-bit sample stamp at part+0x3a0/0x3a4 is increased by 16. Read in full.

name: Voice__trigger
description: Voice__trigger, per-voice vtable +16, starts a note (a2 voice, a3 note, a4 previous note, a5 velocity, a6 low-byte start-mode flag passed by VoiceSlot__start at 0x42014b18). Clears fast-fade/control flags, primes next control tick, records q-dependent independent random offsets at voice+0x28 (wave scan), +0x2c (cutoff), +0x30 (oscillator-1 pitch), initializes glide/velocity/wave-number state and parameter ramps, and clamps modulated envelope A/D/S/R values. The three envelope restart decisions use the exact Boolean ((int)partFloat[+0xe4] == 1) OR ((a6 & 255) != 0); on restart each envelope enters attack stage 1 and resets its stage timer, with equal-current-target cases proceeding to stage 2; on the nonrestart path stages 2..4 are retained and other stages are put into 2. Independently a6 nonzero clears oscillator phase and marks both wave caches dirty, whereas a6 zero uses table-change comparisons to set dirty flags. The note/previous-note, part glide control and held-note table drive glide timing independently. Computes both LP and HP mode-specific cutoff, resonance, normalization and four feedback weights from the two approximated one-pole reciprocal stage factors, using bit-seeded reciprocal B(x) (see Round 99 and VOICE_DSP_MATH.md); LP feedback gain uses 2*r and HP 1.2*r, with mode-specific 0.8 and 0.85 resonance scalings. Re-points and initializes the mod matrix and both LFO connections. All stated arithmetic and conditional paths were checked statically; external meanings of several part flags and physical sound behavior are not inferred. Portamento is separately controlled by GlideRate at part parameter float offset +0x40 and GlideMode at +0x44. With GlideRate below 0.01, the starting pitch is the new note. With rate >=0.01, GlideMode 0 allows glide directly; a nonzero mode allows glide only if a held note OTHER than the incoming note appears in the 128-note table at manager+0x62c. Where enabled, voice current pitch starts at previous note and the stored positive pitch step is (abs(newNote-previousNote)/(3*44100*GlideRate^3))*128; otherwise current pitch starts at new note. This is distinct from the start/retrigger byte a6 controlling envelopes and oscillator resets. Round 104: At 0x4037bef9..0x4037bf1f, on note start the separate pan ramp at voice+0x4e0 takes the part Pan word (part parameter offset +212) into current and target and sets counter to zero; the volume ramp at +0x4d0 takes the square of part Volume float (+220) into current and target, resetting the counter. No claim is made that all later pan/volume modulation remains constant.

name: Voice__render
description: Voice__render, per-voice vtable +36, renders 16-sample mono synth buffer into stereo float output with optional cycle profiling. Control ticks compare voice+0x5bc against the shared tick, and update free/clocked LFO speed, optional active LFO objects, mod matrix, clamped wave/amp/filter envelope A/D/S/R and the three stage-1..6 envelope machines. The q-dependent envelope scheduling path either steps per tick or on eligible eighth ticks; a separate tick/voice-flag path bypasses expensive control updates. Ramps update current, step, target and signed count for oscillator volumes, noise, volume and pan. The audio path updates wavetable selections and expands 64-byte unsigned halfwaves into 128 signed samples by forward (byte-128) and reverse inverted (127-byte) halves; four LX7 SALT instructions at 0x4037d038, 0x4037d160, 0x4037d307 and 0x4037d430 compare wave-row index >60 and select table 88 for rows 61..63, otherwise the selected table. Two oscillators read the top 7 phase bits with no adjacent-sample interpolation; noise uses the 0x41c64ed1/0x329d LCG and seven shape branches. Filter modes 0/1 use four low-pass one-pole states (second/fourth tap), 2/3 use high-pass states (fourth/second tap); all four use explicit precomputed resonance feedback weights and soft saturation S(z)=z*B(abs(z)+bias), with B a float-bit-seeded approximate reciprocal refined once (see Round 99). LP subtracts weighted state feedback, HP adds it; LP mode 1 scales resonance by 0.8 and HP mode 3 by 0.85; mode-dependent post gains are 0.75 LP and 1.2 HP. Mode 4 uses Drive__shapeChannel with the cutoff-controlled amount, quadratic post gain and dry-addition threshold. Other modes bypass filter shaping. Applies amp envelope, voice gain, and complementary quadratic pan gains p*(2-p) and (1-p)*(1+p) to 16 left and right float samples. The coefficient-change gate, waveform refresh conditions and all local exit branches are traced; external table contents and acoustic transfer response are not inferred. LFO boundary finding: clamp to [0,18] at 0x4037c0c2..0x4037c0d4 and 0x4037c153..0x4037c164; only 18 floats are initialized by Voice__init, so selection 18 reads the first float of the separate interpolator coefficient table starting at 0x3fcbb4c0. No claim that the UI generates 18 or that the audible result has been tested. On render control updates, current voice pitch at +0x1c approaches target pitch at +0x20 by positive step +0x24, clamped on overshoot (0x4037cd3c..0x4037cd73). Both clocked-LFO index expressions first convert their per-part ratio float (+0x9c or +0xb0) to double, add 0.05, truncate and clamp to 0..18. Ordinary stepped UI descriptors supply 18 choices 0..17; index 18 can be reached only by a nonstandard/out-of-range stored value (>=17.95) through an unvalidated parameter path, not through normal pot/encoder edits. The raw setter and stored-sound transfer do not enforce the step bound. No hardware malfunction claim is made. Wavetable buffer consumer now confirmed: voice+56 and voice+204 reference shared VoiceEngine descriptors (+20 and +0x201c). Each descriptor holds the main cache pointer at +0, cached table number at +4, and a 64-row x 128-byte decoded bank at +8 (shared+28 or shared+0x2024). On a table-number mismatch, the renderer rebuilds that entire bank from cache halfwaves, stores the selected table at descriptor+4, and copies the chosen 128-byte row from descriptor+8+128*row into an oscillator-local playback buffer. The read/copy loops occur at 0x4037d08c..0x4037d096 and 0x4037d1b5..0x4037d1bf, and on the alternate render paths at 0x4037d35c..0x4037d366 and 0x4037d485..0x4037d48f. If the table has not changed, the bank refresh is bypassed. These prove the consumers that earlier rounds described as unidentified.

name: VoiceEngine__controlTick
description: Per-block tick of the shared DSP object (a2; vtable offset 16, called by VoiceManager__render for the object at part+4). Position +0x4024 += 16 (a wrap adds 65 to the deadline); when it reaches the deadline +0x4028 the control tick count +0x402c is increased and the deadline += 49 (plus a random value -32 to +30 when q > 0.25, q = the float at *(object+0x10)+0x50, null gives 0). Then it converts the tempo from the clock record at +0x4068 (the double at record+8) to a float with ROM 0x4000252c and compares it with the previous tempo (+0x4070); when the tempo changed or the dirty bytes +0x406c / +0x406d are set it recomputes the rates of the two shared LFOs: if LFO1Clocked (array [a2+12] + 160) is 0 the rate is Speed squared (+152), otherwise tempo times the entry of the 19 float ratio table at 0x3fcbb478 selected by trunc(LFO1Ratio (+156) + 0.05) limited to 0..18; the result goes to the LFO rate field at +0x4038; LFO2 uses +172, +176, +180 and +0x4054. Finally, when LFO1Sync (+168) or LFO2Sync (+188) is above 0 the shared LFO is advanced with Lfo__updateGlobal (0x42016648) on +0x4030 or +0x404c, with the argument ((tick count and 3) == 0). Read in full; the contents of the ratio table (filled at run time) were not found in the image.

name: ModMatrix__evaluate
description: Mod matrix evaluator (a2 = ModMatrix object at voice+0x5e0; this address was wrongly classed as library). Increments the u16 tick stamp at +0x244. Then for each of the 8 rows (8 bytes from +0x204: byte source id, byte destination id, float amount at +4): skips when the destination id is above 26 or 0; the destination record is +0x12c + 8*dest; if its u16 stamp (+6) differs from the current stamp it clears the accumulator (word +0) and takes the stamp; skips when the source id is 0 or the source pointer (word at +0x14 + 8*src) is null; x = amount*2 - 1; if the destination flag byte (record +4) is non-zero x = x*|x|; accumulator = accumulator + source value * x, clamped to -100..+100. Confirmed from code: the flag is the curved-amount switch (set for Pitch, O1 Pch, O2 Pch). A destination that no row touches in a tick keeps its old accumulator; any clearing elsewhere was not checked. Source ids above 34 are not range-checked here (the UI offers 0 to 34).

name: VoiceManager__noteOff
description: Part note-off (a2 = part, a3 = note, a4 forwarded to voice release). Ignores note >127. Writes part+0x62c+note = 2 while sustain-pedal byte +0x398 is active, else 0. Scans all eight 112-byte voice slots in order determined by signed round-robin byte +0x390: when active slot state +17 is 1 and note at +18 matches, it changes state to 2, copies the two release timestamp words from part+0x3a0/+0x3a4 into slot+40/+44, and invokes DSP vtable +20, except while sustain or mono byte +0x397 is active. If state is 3 and pending note at slot+32 matches, sets pending-release flag slot+38 and stores a4 into slot+37. In mono mode, when a matching slot was found, scans the 128-entry held-note table from note 127 downward and excludes the released note; if another note is held, invokes the part note-on method with that note and saved velocity from part+0x396; otherwise releases the matched voice. All paths and offsets checked in disassembly.

name: Task__notifyTake
description: FreeRTOS ulTaskGenericNotifyTake(a2 = notification index, a3 = clear count on exit, a4 = ticks to wait), called by the engine task with (0, 1, -1) = wait forever and clear the count. name: AudioOut__processBlock
description: One 16-frame output step (a2 = engine object 0x3fca3974, a3 = int32 left output, a4 = int32 right output). Calls Fx__process(engine+0x188, the six buses, gain) and converts bus 0 left and right to int32 by multiplying by 2^31 (0x4f000000) with a saturating float-to-int64 conversion clamped to the int32 range. Then it runs the LFO LED generator (see below) and, when the measure byte at engine+0x1698 is set, updates the average and peak at engine+0 and engine+4 from the elapsed microseconds (same 0.05 / 0.95 filter). LFO LED generator: a software LFO at engine+0x1618..0x1648 (output s16 +24, phase u16 +26, last compared phase u16 +28, wrap flag byte +30, rate float +32, skew float +40 times 65535, shape byte +44, output float +48); every fourth control tick (a counter at +124 and a deadline at +132 advancing 49 samples per tick, counter at +128) it advances the phase by trunc(rate x 127 x 64) limited to 0x1fff, using shapes 0 sine (1024-entry table 0x3c06ed94, interpolated), 1 triangle, 2 square, 3 and 4 ramps, 5 noise (ROM random), 6 sample and hold; the LED word at 0x3fcd1dd4 (board+0x25c) is set when the output exceeds 0.5. name: Fx__process
description: FX chain for one block of 16 samples per channel (a2 = FX object, a3 = bus 0 left, a4 = bus 0 right, a5/a6 = bus 1 left/right, a7 and the first stack word = bus 2 left/right, one stack float = modulation input passed to the effects). Buffers are 16 floats; the code works in four groups of four samples. Chain: if the FX1 slot pointer (+0x1488) is not null it calls the effect process (vtable +0x10) on bus 0 into a temporary, otherwise copies bus 0; adds bus 1; runs FX2 (+0x148c, same call) unless it is null or equal to FX1 (then the signal is passed through); adds bus 2; applies a direct-form-I biquad on each channel (coefficients +0x60 feedback on y[n-1], +0x64 feedback on y[n-2], +0x68 b0, +0x6c b1, +0x70 b2; state words alternate between two slots so there is no shifting; left state +0x74..+0x80, right +0x84..+0x90; b0 = 1 and the rest 0 after Fx__init, so it is a pass-through unless something writes the coefficients, and no other writer was found); then a peak limiter per group of four samples (peak = max of the absolute values over both channels, envelope += (peak - env) * (+8 attack when rising, else +0xc release), target gain = 0.85 / env when env > threshold +0x10 else 1.0, gain += +0x14 * (target - gain), applied to both channels); finally Fx__clipBlock on the left and on the right buffer. Bus meaning by the destination setting: bus 0 FX1 then FX2, bus 1 FX2 only, bus 2 direct. [Stage 16: hook at 0x4200f297 inserts the Flavour compressor after EQ and before the peak limiter; limiter pointer fix at 0x4200f550/0x4200f556.]

Table object 0x3fcd65d8 entry 1 (pointer at +8, length at +12): index < 0 gives the first entry, index >= length - 1 gives the last entry, otherwise linear interpolation between the two neighbours. name: Compressor__process
description: Compressor effect process for one block (a2 = object, a3/a4 = input left/right, a5/a6 = output left/right, a7 = float added to the threshold ramp value, a stack float added to the ratio ramp value). Each call first advances the ramps (current += step, counter - 1, snap to the target at 0). InGain dB = -30 + 60 * v, OutGain dB = -30 + 60 * v (each converted with Db__toLinear only when the ramp value changed, cached at +0x78 / +0x7c; results +0x70 and +0x74). Threshold: t = clamp(ramp + a7, 0, 1), dB = (1 - t) * -50, linear via Db__toLinear (stored dB +0x68, linear +0x6c), sets the recompute byte +0x81. Ratio = 1 + 99 * r^3 with r = clamp(ramp + stack float, 0, 1), stored at +0x8c. Then calls Compressor__kernel four times (state at +0x4c) for the four groups of four samples, and keeps a copy of the output block at +0x3c0 (left) and +0x400 (right) (consumer not found). It resets the gain-history index +0x3bc to 0 at every block. [Stage 16: also processes the Flavour compressor each block (CustomCompressorHW__stereoProcess).]

name: Chorus__process
description: Chorus process for one block of 16 samples (a2 = object, a3/a4 = input left/right, a5/a6 = output left/right, a7 = float added to DryWet, a stack float added to Depth; Fx__process passes 0 as the stack float). Read in full. Steps: (1) advances the Center ramp (+0x24) and Depth ramp (+0x34) one step per block call. (2) Depth in samples = clamp(depth + stack float + optional source at +0x48, 0, 1)^3 * 882; base = 2 + 0.2 * 44100 * center^2 + depth samples. (3) LFO rate = 0.001 + 20 * clamp(speed + optional source at +0x4c, 0, 1)^2 (stored per block; per-sample table step = rate * (1 + offset * spread) * 1024 / 44100 with a four-entry offset table at 0x3c06ff60 = 0, 0.075, -0.047, 0.097; the right-channel LFO phase is the left phase plus spread * 0.5 * 1024 table positions). (4) Shape (+0x1c4): 0 = triangle, 1 = sine read from table entry 0 of 0x3fcd65d8 without interpolation (nearest entry; observed), other values give a constant 0 (no modulation). The number of voices per channel is Stages index + 1 (index 0..3 = 1..4, UI labels 2/4/6/8 count both channels). Voice i delay in samples = base + i * spread * 882 + lfo * depth samples, smoothed per voice by a ramp (step = (new target - current) / 100, advanced per sample, re-targeted each block). (5) Per sample and channel the delay read position is the write index minus trunc(delay) (limited to 0..11910) with two-tap linear interpolation between neighbouring buffer entries; the buffers are 11,911 floats (47,644 bytes) per channel with a wrap by multiplication magic 0x6023137f; the sum of all voice taps is the wet signal. (6) The delay input is the input run through a one-pole low-pass (High Cut) and a low-cut stage (both before the buffer, states +0x1d4 and +0x1ec shared by left and right), plus Feedback * the last voice tap, with Feedback = clamp(feedback + optional source at +0x50, 0, 1) * 1.96 - 0.98; filter coefficients are expf(-pi * x^3), where x = 1 - HighCut or LowCut. The exponent path first multiplies x^3 by float 0.5, then by double -2*pi, so the prior expf(-pi*0.5*x^3) description contained an extra factor (Round 93). (7) Dry/Wet: m = clamp(DryWet + a7 + optional source at +0x44, 0, 1); targets wet = 2m - m^2 and dry = 1 - m^2, ramped linearly over the 16 samples (step = (target - current) / 16, current values at +0x1fc wet and +0x1f8 dry); output = dry * input + wet * voice sum. (8) After the loop an output level compensation g = 1 - 0.13 * stage index, minus 0.25 * fb when fb > 0, plus 0.2 * fb when fb < 0 (fb = the -0.98..0.98 value), clamped 0..1, scale = 1 - (1 - g) * wet gain, multiplies ALL 16 samples of both outputs (the older note that said only indices 0, 4, 8, 12 was wrong; all four unrolled loops cover the full block). A per-channel clear flag (bytes +0xf8 / +0x11c side) zeroes the delay buffer 32 floats per sample until it is empty. The reset routine sets byte +0x200 to 1; this process clears it to 0 at the common exit, both when the compensation scale equals 1 and after multiplying all 32 output samples otherwise (0x4201086f-0x4201092b). No extra compensation is applied at unity. The external purpose of this byte is not asserted. Optional +0x44 DryWet, +0x48 Depth, +0x4c Speed and +0x50 Feedback pointers each read a float only if nonnull and add it to the named control before the corresponding clamp or feedback mapping.

name: Delay__process
description: Delay process for one block of 16 samples (a2 = object, a3/a4 = input left/right, a5/a6 = output left/right, a7 = float added to DryWet, a stack float added to Feedback). Read in full; some arithmetic is only partly interpreted (flagged). Buffers are 441,000 floats per channel (read/write index wrap at 441000 using a multiplication magic); per-sample tap distances are clamped to 0..440999 before integer and fractional read offsets are formed (0x42010f86-0x42011016). (1) Time per channel: free mode (Synced byte +0x48 = 0): ramps advance once per block, then t = 1 + 88200 * clamp(ramp + optional source * 0.1, 0, 1)^2 samples (so about 1 sample to 2.0 s); with Link +0x44 above 0.1 the right time is derived from the left time (plus the word +0x40 * 4410 samples; that word is 0 after the constructor and its writer was not found: unconfirmed). Synced mode: time = ratio * beat length + optional source * 8820 where ratio = table 0x3c06ffd0 [0.125, 0.1667, 0.1875, 0.25, 0.3333, 0.375, 0.5, 0.6667, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.3333, 1.5, 1.6667, 1.75, 2.0] indexed by RatioL (+0x4c) or RatioR (+0x50) and beat length is a double of samples-per-beat from the TempoClock pointer at +0xfc (clock+24, converted to float; TempoClock computes 44100 x 60 / BPM), clamped to 1..88200 samples, NaN gives 1.0. (2) The current delay moves toward its target by (target - current) * 0.000125 per sample (a slow slew, applied per sample inside the block) and is split into integer and fraction for a two-tap linear interpolated read. (3) The signal read from the buffer is passed through a DC blocker (coefficients 0.99, 1, -1), then a High Cut one-pole low-pass and a Low Cut stage with coefficient t = expf(-pi * x^3), x = 1 - HighCut or LowCut, inside the feedback loop. The float 0.5 preceding the double -2*pi multiplication was previously counted twice (Round 93). (4) Feedback gain = clamp(Feedback + stack float + optional source, 0, 1) squared. (5) Exact per-sample stereo routing verified at 0x42011244-0x420112f7: let x be float parameter +0x34 (constructor default 0.7), A=(1-x)^4, B=1-A, H=B/2, and p=clamp(Feedback + stack argument + optional source,0,1)^2. Let uL,uR be the current raw inputs and yL,yR the two delayed taps after DC blocker, HighCut one-pole low-pass and LowCut subtraction. Left buffer write = (1-H)*uL + H*uR + p*(A*yL + B*yR). Right buffer write = A*uR + p*(B*yL + A*yR). There is no direct uL term in the right buffer write. Cross-mixing is based on x, while feedback gain p comes from separate +0x30 control. Both writes are clamped to [-100,100]. (6) The DC blocker is y = tap - previousTap + 0.99*previousOutput, updated separately for left/right at object +0xb0..+0xc8. Each channel then computes highcutLP = (1-h)*y + h*oldHighcut and lowcutLP = (1-l)*highcutLP + l*oldLowcut, and uses bandpass = highcutLP - lowcutLP, where h and l are expf(-pi*(1-HighCut)^3) and expf(-pi*LowCut^3). Filter coefficients at subobjects +0xcc/+0xe4 and per-channel state offsets +0xc and +0x14 are used. (7) Delay tap read interpolation is frac*buffer[write-trunc(delay)-1] + (1-frac)*buffer[write-trunc(delay)], using the 441000-entry circular buffers and a per-sample 0.000125 slew from current delay toward its target. Current tap and DC-filter results equal to positive or negative infinity are zeroed by explicit tests; no equivalent NaN test is seen in those branches. (8) DryWet m=clamp(+0x2c + a7 + optional source +0x58,0,1) gives dry target=1-m^2 and wet target=2m-m^2, advanced from cached +0x100/+0x104 toward targets in 16 equal per-sample steps (or set immediately when reset flag +0x108 is set). Outputs are dry*uL + wet*yL and dry*uR + wet*yR, where yL and yR are post-filter delay taps BEFORE stereo feedback mixing. (9) Clear bytes +0x84/+0xa8 zero their respective ring buffers 32 samples per processed sample, and the reset flag +0x108 is cleared at the end. Hardware routing and any external writer of static word +0x40 remain unconfirmed. The external TempoClock double at +0xfc points to samples-per-beat, as established in Round 103.
time formatter (vt 0x3c06fd60 and 0x3c06fd80): t = 2*x^2 + 2.27e-5 s; if t < 0.1 prints "%.3f ms" (t*1000), otherwise "%.3f s"

name: Drive__shape
description: Drive waveshaper for 16 samples (a2 = shaper state of one channel, a3 = input, a4 = output). State: +0 output level (from the table 0x3c07002c, 0.2 for types 0..4), +4 drive amount (already squared), +8 previous input sample, +0xc type index. Pre-gain p = amount^2 * 128. Per type: 1 and 2 and 4 and 0 use s = input + previous input (two-point sum, previous = input); type 1: u = 0.7071 + s * p, output = 2 * level * (u^2 - 0.5) for 0 < u < 1, -level for u <= 0, +level for u >= 1 (hard limits); type 2: u = 0.7071 + s * p, w = min(u^2 - 0.5, 0.5), output = 4 * level * (w - w * |w|); type 3 (no history): v = max(input * p, -1), output = level * min(v^2 + 2v, 1); type 4: v = s * p, f = frac(v) (v - trunc(v), +1 when negative), z = 2f - 1, output = 4 * level * (z - z * |z|); type 0 (default branch): v = s * p, output = level * (-1 if v < -1, v^2 + 2v if -1 <= v < 0, 2v - v^2 if 0 <= v <= 1, +1 if v > 1). Which type index carries which UI name (PNP, Tube, PickUp, Diode, Crunch) is not derivable from the code (the labels come from display code; unconfirmed mapping).

name: Drive__shapeChannel
description: Drive per-channel wrapper (a2 = shaper state, a3 = input block, a4 = output block, or 0 for in-place). When the squared drive amount (state +4) is at least 0.125 it simply calls Drive__shape. Below 0.125 it keeps a copy of the input scaled by w = (0.125 - amount^2) * 8, runs Drive__shape, and adds the scaled input to the output so that very low Amount fades to a clean pass-through (output = shaped + w * input).

Amount = clamp(Amount + stack float + optional source +0x1c, 0, 1), squared and written to both shaper states (+0x2c, +0x3c). name: EQ__updateCoefficients
description: EQ coefficient update (a2 = EQ object), called by EQ__process when the dirty byte +0x13c is set; clears the byte at the end. Let e = clamp(+0xf4 + +0x144, 0, 1) - 0.5 (frequency offset, 0 with the usual parameters) and m = clamp(DryWet +0xec + +0x140, 0, 1) (stored +0x130). Output gain dB = (Gain +0xf0 - 0.5) * 40 * m (stored +0x138), linear via Db__toLinear into +0x134. Bands (a frequency in Hz becomes f / 44100): Low shelf: x = clamp(e + LowFreq), frequency = 2^(4.9068 + 3.9068 * x) (30 to 450 Hz), gain dB = (LowGain - 0.5) * 40 * m, calls EQ__lowShelf on the filter at +0xc. Mid 1: frequency = 2^(7.644 + 5.1517 * x) (200 to 7000 Hz), gain dB = (MidGain - 0.5) * 40 * m, Q = 2^(-3.3219 + 7.3219 * MidQ) (0.1 to 16), calls EQ__peaking on the filter at +0x44. Mid 2: same with Mid2Freq / Mid2Gain / Mid2Q on the filter at +0x7c. High shelf: frequency = 2^(10.6887 + 3.7172 * x) (1.65 kHz to 20 kHz), gain dB = (HighGain - 0.5) * 40 * m, calls EQ__highShelf on the filter at +0xb4. A NaN frequency value falls back to the lowest frequency of that band. The Dry/Wet parameter therefore scales all band and output gains in dB rather than mixing dry and wet.

name: EQ__process

The value +0x140 = a7 + optional float read through the pointer +0x148, and +0x144 = stack float + optional float through +0x14c; if either changed the dirty byte is set. When dirty it calls EQ__updateCoefficients. The inputs are copied to the outputs and then the four biquads (low shelf, mid 1, mid 2, high shelf) run in place on left (Eq__blockFilter_a) and right (Eq__blockFilter_b) when their band word (+0xf8, +0x104, +0x114, +0x124) is above 0.1 (always true after the constructor). Finally both outputs are multiplied by the linear output gain +0x134 unless it equals exactly 1.0.

description: Flanger process for one block of 16 samples (a2 = object, a3/a4 = input left/right, a5/a6 = output left/right, a7 = float added to DryWet, a stack float added to Depth). Read in full. (1) Dry/Wet: m = clamp(DryWet + a7 + optional source +0x24, 0, 1); targets wet = 2m - m^2 and dry = 1 - m^2, ramped over the 16 samples (step (target - current) / 16; current wet +0xac, dry +0xa8). (2) Feedback value v = 2 * clamp(Feedback + optional source +0x30, 0, 1) - 1; signed feedback gain = 1 - (1 - v)^3 for v >= 0 and -1 + (1 - |v|)^3 for v < 0 (range -1..1; both ends reach full scale); a compensation magnitude 0.45 * |gain| is kept. (3) Depth in samples = clamp(Depth + stack float + optional source +0x28, 0, 1)^4 * 1411.2. (4) Speed: rate = 0.001 + 20 * clamp(Speed + optional source +0x2c, 0, 1)^4 (Hz-like value, phase advance per block = rate / 2756.25). Base delay = 1 + 1102.5 * Center^2 samples. (5) LFO, updated once per block: Shape 0 = triangle on a 0..1 phase (left phase +0x7c, right phase +0x88 = left plus PhaseDiff, wrapped), other values = sine read from table entry 0 of 0x3fcd65d8 (entry chosen by +0x9c) at the truncated table position (nearest entry, no interpolation; observed) with phases +0x8c (left) and +0xa0 (right = left + PhaseDiff * 1024). Per channel delay in samples = base + (0.5 + 0.5 * lfo) * depth, clamped to 0..2564, split into an integer part (+0x48 left, +0x6c right) and a fractional weight (+0x3c / +0x40 and +0x60 / +0x64); the delay is constant within a block. (6) Per sample and channel: wet tap = (1 - frac) * buf[w - n] + frac * buf[w - n - 1] with a wrap at 2,613 floats; the buffer input is the dry input plus signed feedback gain * the tap (no filters in the loop); output = dry * input + wet * tap. (7) After the loop the outputs are scaled (all 16 samples of both channels) by 1 - wet gain * 0.45 * |feedback gain|; when that equals 1.0 the run flag +0xb0 is cleared instead (observed; purpose not interpreted). Clear flags +0x54 / +0x78 zero the buffers 32 floats per sample after a reset.

Then: CC1 starts a ramp on record 0x3ec, CC2 on 0x41c, CC4 on 0x3fc, CC11 on 0x40c (ramp: target = value, step = (value - current)/length, ticks left = length); CC64 calls vt +0x2c with (pedal down = value above 63); CC74 with a5 at most 127 stores value/127 in the per-note array at this+0xaac+4*a5; CC120 calls vt +0x54 and CC123 vt +0x50 (all sound off, all notes off per the earlier vtable notes).

name: VoiceSlot__start
description: Starts one of the 8 voice slots (a2 slot, a3 slot number 0 to 7, a4 layer index, a5 layer object from fcn.42016a20, a6 manager word +8, a7 pointer table at manager+0x3a8, stack: per-note array pointers for poly aftertouch (+0x6ac), note pitch bend (+0x8ac) and CC74 (+0xaac), and the CC value array (+0x42c)). Writes slot byte +0 = slot number, voice pointer (+0x2c) = voice pool address 0x3fcaaf78 + (layer*8 + slot)*0x828 (fcn.420162bc), +0x28 = a6, +0x60/+0x64/+0x68 = the three per-note array pointers, clears byte +1, u16 +2 (note number) and words +8, +0x10, +0x14, +0x18, +0x1c. Then calls Voice__init with (voice, slot number, a5, a6, a7, slot+0x30, slot+0x40, slot+0x50, CC array). The three per-note float-array pointers at slot+0x60/+0x64/+0x68 correspond to manager+0x6ac (Poly Aftertouch), +0x8ac (per-note Pitch Bend), +0xaac (CC74/MPE Y). Their attached ramp cells live at slot+0x30/+0x40/+0x50 respectively; see Voice__start.

name: VoiceManager__reset
description: Voice manager reset (vt 0x3c0701b8, a3 = layer index 0 to 3). Clears the stamp pair +0x3a0/+0x3a4 and the six controller ramp records at +0x3cc, +0x3dc, +0x3ec, +0x3fc, +0x40c, +0x41c (words +0, +4 and u16 +12). Zeroes 0x680 bytes from +0x62c (a 128-byte note state table at +0x62c, the per-note arrays at +0x6ac poly aftertouch, +0x8ac note pitch bend, +0xaac CC74 slide, 128 floats each) and the 128-float CC value array at +0x42c. Stores the layer object (fcn.42016a20) at this+4 and calls its virtual slot +8 with (layer object, layer index, manager, word +8). Runs VoiceSlot__start for slots 0 to 7. Sets u16 +0x390 = 0x100 and byte +0x398 = 0. Then for k = 0..82 calls its own VoiceManager__setParam with k and the word at +20 of the voice descriptor for k. That call does not store the value (only k = 57 uses it, as the mono flag), so it makes the layer object and the 8 voices recompute their derived values from the parameter block; it does not load layer defaults into the block. At 0x42014ad1..0x42014ad4 it writes u16 0x0100 to part+0x390 in little-endian memory; this initializes byte +0x390 to 0 and byte +0x391 to 1 (the latter is the voice-steal selection flag read by VoiceManager__noteOn). The earlier claim that reset does not initialize +0x391 was incorrect.

name: Voice__start
description: Voice slot start with glide set-up (a2 = voice slot object, a3 = note, a4 = previous note, a5 = velocity byte, a6 = start-mode/retrigger flag, distinct from the GlideMode parameter, 64-bit trigger timestamp on the stack). Sets slot+1 = 1 (playing), s16 +2 = note, byte +4 = velocity, +8 = 0 (age), stamps +16/+20 with the timestamp, and loads the targets of three per-note tables (pointers at slot+96, +100, +104) into +52, +68 and +84. Without the glide flag the current values +48, +64, +80 take the targets at once and the counters (s16 +60, +76, +92) are cleared; with it each counter takes the length in blocks from s16 +62, +78, +94 and the steps +56, +72, +88 = (target - current) / length (ROM float divide). Finally calls the voice DSP object (slot+44) vtable offset 16 with (note, previous note, velocity, glide flag). Read in full; what the three tables and the DSP side do with the values was not traced here. The source pointers at slot+96/+100/+104 refer respectively to the manager per-note Poly Aftertouch, Note Pitch Bend, and CC74/MPE Y float arrays. Their ramp-cell reload lengths were initialized to 10 blocks by VoiceManager__ctor. Flag 0 snaps these controller ramps to target; flag nonzero interpolates current-to-target over the initialized count. This flag is not the independent GlideMode selector of the DSP pitch portamento.

name: VoiceManager__ctor
description: Voice manager constructor (vtable 0x3c0701a8). +4 and +8 = 0; 8 slots of 0x70 bytes from +0x10, each with three ramp cells at slot +0x30, +0x40, +0x50 zeroed except word +12 = 0xa0000. Byte +0x392 = 8, word +0x394 = 0x64003c (bytes 3c 00 64 00; byte +0x397 is the mono flag), byte +0x398 = 0, +0x3a0/+0x3a4 = 0, +0x3c0, +0x3c4, +0x3c8 = 0, word +0xcac = 0 (later set to the global parameter array by fcn.4201476c). Six controller ramp records of 16 bytes: {current float, target float, step float, u16 ticks left, u16 length}: 0x3cc Pitch Bend (length 10), 0x3dc Channel Pressure, 0x3ec Mod Wheel CC1, 0x3fc CC4 (source Pedal), 0x40c Expression CC11, 0x41c Breath CC2 (length 100 each). Pointer table at +0x3a8 lists them in the order 0x3cc, 0x3ec, 0x3dc, 0x3fc, 0x40c, 0x41c. Boundary correction: this constructor initializes +0x392, +0x394 and +0x398 but contains no direct store to the steal-selection byte at part+0x391, which is read by VoiceManager__noteOn. VoiceManager__reset later writes +0x391 as the high byte of its halfword store at +0x390; this constructor contains no direct store.

name: Engine__readParam
description: Engine vtable offset 60. Returns 0 when a3 is above 0x1e0, otherwise the float or word at engine+0x32ec+4 x a3 (the engine parameter array). Read in full; no direct caller found.

name: Engine__noteOn
description: Engine vtable offset 20 (a2 = engine, a3 = note, a4 = velocity, a5 = extra argument, a6 = part selector). Routing from the floats LayerMode (engine+0x3324) and LayerAlloc (engine+0x3328): with LayerMode 3 or less, or LayerAlloc 0, every active part (active byte at part+0xcb0, parts at engine+8 + 0xcb8 p) whose index equals the selector (or all when the selector is -1) gets VoiceManager__noteOn(part, note, velocity, a5, -1). With LayerMode 4 and LayerAlloc 1 the next active part after the byte at engine+0x32e8 is chosen (round robin), 2 adds a random number (0x4203fe88) to that index first, 3 uses the part given by a5 when it is below 4 and active. Read in full.

name: Engine__setSustain
description: Engine vtable 0x3c070218 slot +44 (sustain pedal broadcast; args a3 pedal flag byte, a4 layer or -1). For each of the four layer voice managers (engine+8, stride 0xcb8) whose index equals a4, or for all when a4 is -1, calls VoiceManager__setSustain (fcn.4204e728) with the flag and -1. Read from the code.

name: Part__activeVoiceCount
description: Counts voices in use over the four layers (engine vtable 0x3c070218 slot +52): for each layer i (voice manager at engine+8 + i x 0xcb8) whose active byte (engine + 0xcb8 x (i + 1)) is non-zero and where the layer argument a3 equals i or is -1 (all layers), adds VoiceManager__busySlotCount (fcn.4204e808). Returns the sum. Read from the code.

name: Engine__setPolyphony
description: Engine vtable slot +56: for each layer voice manager whose index equals the layer argument a4, or all when a4 is -1, calls VoiceManager__setPolyphony (fcn.4204e824) with the limit a3. Read from the code.

name: LayerSet__broadcast_c
description: vt 0x3c07026c: calls fcn.4204e7b8 on the four layer sub-objects at this+8, +0xcc0, +0x1978 and +0x2630 (stride 0xcb8). Corrected: the earlier text gave +0xcc8, +0x1980, +0x2638.

name: Engine__setLayerWord3c0
description: Engine vtable slot +68 (engine event 7): calls the setter fcn.4204e834 (stores a3 at layer+0x3c0) on the four layer voice managers (engine+8, +0xcc0, +0x1978, +0x2630). What the value means (notes line 259 guess: Transpose) is unconfirmed. Read from the code.

name: Engine__setLayerWord3c4
description: Engine vtable slot +72 (engine event 8): calls the setter fcn.4204e83c (stores the word a3 at layer+0x3c4) on the four layer voice managers. The notes say the engine passes event value x 0.01 as a float (guess: master tune in cents, unconfirmed). Read from the code.

name: Engine__setLayerFlag3c8
description: Engine vtable slot +76 (engine event 9): calls VoiceLayer__setFlag_3c8 (fcn.4204e844, byte a3) on the four layer voice managers. What the flag means (notes line 259 guess: MPE status) is unconfirmed. Read from the code.

name: Engine__allNotesOff
description: Engine vtable slot +80: calls VoiceManager__allNotesOff (fcn.4204e770) on the four layer voice managers (engine+8, +0xcc0, +0x1978, +0x2630). Read from the code.

Engine vtable slot +12: UI/engine parameter id (a3) to the 32-byte descriptor record (name, label, steps, enum labels, default, flags, formatter). Ids 0..20 give entry id of the table at 0x3c071f54; ids 21..148 (the 128 sequencer step parameters) give entry 21 + ((id - 21) and 3), so the step parameters share four descriptors; ids above 148 are sound parameters: layer q = (id - 149) / 83 and index r = (id - 149) mod 83, and the descriptor comes from the first layer voice manager (engine+8) through its slot fcn.4204e6e4 with r. This is the ParamMgr__getDescriptor of the notes. Read from the code.

name: Part__noteOffToLayers
description: Engine method (vt 0x3c070230): args a3, a4, a5 (layer value), a6 (layer filter, -1 = all). If global parameter 15 (the float at this+0x32ec+60) truncates to 3 - LayerAlloc, whose choices are Layered, Round Robin, Random Robin, Midi Split, so 3 is Midi Split - only when a5 is below 4 and the active byte of layer a5 (byte at this+0xcb8*(a5+1)) is set it calls fcn.40380afc(manager of layer a5 at this+8+0xcb8*a5, a3, a4, a5, -1) (identified as the voice manager note-off in Round 48). Otherwise it calls the same function for every active layer 0 to 3 where a6 equals the layer index or is -1, with a5 as the fourth argument.

name: Engine__controlChange
description: Engine vtable offset 28 (a2 = engine, a3 = CC, a4 = value, a5 = extra, a6/a7 = part selector). With LayerAlloc (engine+0x3328) equal to 3 only the part given by a6 (below 4 and active) gets VoiceManager__controlChange; otherwise every active part whose index equals the selector, or all when the selector is -1. Read in full.

name: Engine__channelPressure
description: Engine vtable offset 32. Same routing as Engine__controlChange (LayerAlloc 3: the part named by the selector, otherwise all active parts or the selected one) calling VoiceManager__channelPressure (0x420147f4) with (value, note index, -1). Read in full.

name: Engine__polyAftertouch
description: Engine vtable offset 36. Same routing as Engine__channelPressure, calling VoiceManager__polyAftertouch (0x42014738) on the chosen parts. Read in full.

name: Engine__pitchBend
description: Engine vtable offset 40. Same routing as Engine__channelPressure, calling VoiceManager__pitchBend (0x42014788) on the chosen parts. Read in full.

name: Engine__mixdown
description: Engine vtable offset 96 (a2 = engine, a3 to a7 and a sixth pointer = the six 16-float bus buffers, stack argument = transport record). Clears all six buffers, then for part 0..3 (parts at engine+8 + 0xcb8 p, selected by the active byte part+0xcb0): renders the part with VoiceManager__render(part, temporary left, temporary right) and reads the part's Destination float (engine+0x3620 + 0x14c p) rounded with +0.05: 1 adds the part output to the second stereo bus, 2 to the third, anything else to the first. The additions are done four floats at a time over the 16 samples. Read in full; the display names of the Destination values (Out, FX1, FX2) are not matched here.

name: Engine__setLayerMode
description: Applies LayerMode (a2 = engine). Calls VoiceManager__allSoundOff on the four parts, then reads LayerMode (float at engine+0x3324, rounded with +0.05). Mode 4 (Multi): each part's active byte (part+0xcb0, that is engine+0xcb8 + 0xcb8 p) is set to 1 when its ActiveInMulti float (engine+0x3688, +0x37d4, +0x3920, +0x3a6c) is above 0, the active parts are counted (n) and every one of the four parts gets the polyphony 8 / n (1 when n is 0) through VoiceManager__setPolyphony. Modes 0 to 3 (single layer): the part with the same index as the mode becomes active with polyphony 8, the others become inactive and get polyphony 0, which VoiceManager__setPolyphony ignores (it accepts 1 to 8 only), so their old limit stays. Read in full; the caller (the engine parameter setter) was not re-checked here.

name: Engine__setParam
description: Engine parameter set (a2 = engine object, a3 = id, a4 = float value). Stores the value at this+0x32ec+4*id for every id (481 floats: 149 global ids, then 4 layers x 83 sound parameters, so the layer blocks are at +0x3540 + 0x14c*layer, 0x14c = 83*4); for id 14 (LayerMode) calls fcn.420156d8 only when the value changed; for ids 149 to 480 it computes layer = (id-149)/83 and k = (id-149) mod 83 and calls the layer's VoiceManager__setParam (engine+8+0xcb8*layer) with (k, value); for k = 82 (ActiveInMulti) it calls fcn.420156d8 instead. Global ids 0 to 148 are only stored. It does not validate values against discrete parameter step counts. An out-of-range LFO ratio float is stored unchanged and is visible to the Voice__render clocked-LFO index conversion.

name: ParamMgr__loadDefaults
description: Loads defaults (virtual slot +0x10 of the engine object with vtable 0x3c070218; the four layer managers sit at +8 + 0xcb8*i). For global parameter ids 0 to 148 it takes the descriptor (getDescriptor 0x42014f7c: 0 to 20 from 0x3c071f54, 21 and up repeating the 4 SeqStep rows) and writes the word at descriptor +20 through setParam (default Engine__setParam, which stores into the float array at this+0x32ec; when id 14 (LayerMode) changes it calls fcn.420156d8). Layer sound parameters (ids 149 and up) are not set here. Then for layers 0 to 3 it sets manager word +8 to this+0x3540+0x14c*i (the layer's block of 83 floats, see Engine__setParam), runs VoiceManager__reset(layer i) and calls fcn.4201476c directly to store the pointer this+0x32ec at manager +0xcac. Descriptor +20 is the default value: besides this use, the BPM descriptor holds 0x3e86bca2 = 0.2630, the same value TempoState__init uses for 120 BPM.

name: Voice__release
description: Default voice release (vtable offset 20, a3 = release velocity): stores the velocity / 127 (3c010204) as a float at voice+0x14 and sets the three envelope stage bytes at voice+0x510, +0x530 and +0x550 to 5 (release). Read in full.

name: Voice__descriptorByIndex
description: Voice class virtual slot +8 (vtable 0x3c070290): returns 0x3c072274 + 32 x index for index 0..82, else null. 0x3c072274 is entry 25 of the ParamInfo table 0x3c071f54 (25 x 32 bytes after its start), so these are the 83 per-layer voice parameter entries.

name: Voice__init
description: Voice initialiser (voice vtable 0x3c070288 slot +12; the voice object is 0x828 bytes; earlier text mapped this address to spi_master, wrong). Args: a2 voice, a3 slot number, a4 layer object (manager +4), a5 layer parameter block pointer (manager word +8 = engine+0x3540+0x14c*layer), a6 pointer table (manager +0x3a8), a7 ramp cell 0 (slot+0x30), stack: ramp cell 1 (slot+0x40), ramp cell 2 (slot+0x50), CC value array (manager+0x42c). Stores slot number at voice+4, the layer object at +8, the parameter block pointer at +0x5b8, the pointer table at +0x5cc, ramp cells at +0x5d0/+0x5d4/+0x5d8 and the CC array at +0x5dc. The ModMatrix at voice+0x5e0 (0x248 bytes, ends at the voice end) gets its source cells through ModMatrix__setSource: 1 Wav Env voice+0x4f8; 2 Filt Env +0x538; 3 Amp Env +0x518; 4 LFO1 +0x578; 5 LFO1*MW +0x598; 6 LFO1*AT +0x5a0; 7 LFO2 +0x594; 8 LFO2*MW +0x59c; 9 LFO2*AT +0x5a4; 10 Mod Wheel manager record 0x3ec; 11 Pitch Bend record 0x3cc; 12 Note PB ramp cell 1; 13 Ch Press record 0x3dc; 14 Poly AT ramp cell 0; 15 MPE Y ramp cell 2; 16 Pedal record 0x3fc; 17 Expression record 0x40c; 18 Breath record 0x41c; 19 to 28 CC 22 to CC 31 CC array +88 to +124; 29 Keytrack voice+24; 30 Velocity voice+16; 31 Rel Velo voice+20 (id to cell pairing read from the calls). Then ModMatrix__setDestFlag for destinations 1 to 5 and 9 to 26 (flag 1 for 3, 4 and 5, else 0). First call only (guard: float at 0x3fcbb478 equal to 0) it builds three global tables with ROM float and double math: (1) 18 floats at 0x3fcbb478, entry i = 0.00059725868 / D[i] with D[i] the note length in quarter notes from the 18 doubles at 0x3c0702b0 (16, 12, 8, 4, 3, 2, 1.5, 1, 0.75, 2/3, 0.5, 0.375, 1/3, 0.25, 1/6, 0.125, 1/12, 1/16), one per LFO ratio choice 4/1 to 1/64; read by the LFO rate code as tempo * table[ratio]. (2) 0x3fcbb4c0: 128 rows of 8 floats (32 bytes), row r taps at x = -3 - r/128 + j (j = 0..7), value = sinc * Kaiser window (beta 2, half width 4) with sinc = sin(pi*0.1764*x)/(pi*0.1764*x) (1 at x = 0) and Kaiser = I0(2*sqrt(1-(x/4)^2)) / I0(2), each row divided by its sum. (3) 0x3fcbc4c0: 128 rows of 12 floats (48 bytes), x = -5 - r/128 + j (j = 0..11), same sinc, Kaiser beta 9 and half width 6 (I0(9*sqrt(1-(x/6)^2)) / I0(9)), each row divided by its sum. I0 is summed as a power series until a term is below 1e-31 of the sum. The voice render uses them as fractional-delay interpolation filters: phase bits 17 to 23 pick the row (128 sub-sample steps), bits 24 to 31 the start sample, taps accumulate over a 128-sample ring (index mask 0x7f). Additional verified boundary: initializer writes 18 float ratios at 0x3fcbb478..0x3fcbb4bc, while the LFO renderer clamps its ratio index to 0..18 inclusive; index 18 reads 0x3fcbb4c0, also the start of the neighboring interpolation table. This discrepancy is a potential out-of-bounds ratio lookup, not a hardware-confirmed error. At 0x42015dd1..0x42015dde, Voice__init installs two descriptor pointers in the voice: voice+56 points to shared VoiceEngine+20 and voice+204 points to shared VoiceEngine+0x201c. Their byte banks start at shared+28 and shared+0x2024. These are passed to Voice__render for oscillator waveform refresh and selection.

name: Voice__deletingDtor
description: Deleting destructor (vtable 0x3c07028c): calls operator delete(this, 0x828); 0x828 is the size printed by the console for sizeof(SynthVoice).

name: Lfo__update
description: LFO phase and waveform step, voice copy (a2 = LFO object, a3 = elapsed control ticks, a4 = rate modulation count; called from Voice__render for the LFOs at voice+0x560 and +0x57c). Fields: s16 raw output +0, u16 phase +2, u16 previous phase +4, retrigger byte +6, float rate +8, rate modulation scale +12, skew +16, shape byte +20, float output +24. Step = min(0x1fff, max(0, trunc(rate x 127 x 64 + count x rate x scale x 4))) times the elapsed ticks (ticks forced to 0 when +6 is set); the 16-bit phase advances by the step. Skew: break point = trunc(skew x 65535) at least 1; a phase below it is stretched to 0..32768, above it to 32768..65536. Shapes by byte +20: 0 sine (1024-entry interpolated table at 0x3c070540), 1 triangle, 2 square, 3 falling ramp, 4 rising ramp, 5 white noise (ROM random every update), 6 sample and hold (new random value at phase wrap or on retrigger). Output = raw / 32768 into +24; +4 takes the new phase and +6 is cleared. Read in full; identical to Lfo__updateGlobal except for the sine table address.

name: Voice__fastFade
description: Voice vtable offset 28 (fast fade for steals): writes 0.01 (0x3c23d70a) to the amp envelope release value at voice+0x52c; if the release slot (vtable offset 20) is the default Voice__release it does the same work inline (voice+0x14 = 0, stage bytes at +0x510, +0x530, +0x550 = 5), otherwise it calls that slot with 0; then sets the byte voice+0x5c8 to 1 (the per-block control copy no longer overwrites +0x52c). Read in full.

name: VoicePool__voiceAddress
description: Returns the address of voice i: 0x3fcaaf78 + i x 0x828; the only caller is VoiceSlot__start.

name: VoiceBank__ctor
description: Static constructor of the 32 voice objects (4 layers x 8 voices; base 0x3fcaaf78, stride 0x828, end 0x3fcbb478). For each voice it sets the voice vtable 0x3c070288 and clears or sets several hundred default fields (some constants: 60.0 at +28 and +32, 0.01 at +36, 1.0 at +16, 0.25 and 0.2 at +0x3d8 and +0x3d4, a table of filter constants at voice+0x3e4..0x3fc), sets both LFO skews to 0.5 (voice+0x570 and +0x58c) and the byte voice+5 and voice+0x52 flags, runs the sub-object constructor 0x42017054 on the mod matrix object at voice+0x5e0, and once (guard byte 0x3fccde94) builds the envelope coefficient table at 0x3fccde98: entry i = 1.0 when ROM[i] (u32 at 0x3c070340, 128 entries) is above 0x7ffe, else ROM[i] x 0.0625 / 32767. At the end it registers the destructor 0x4204e898 with __cxa_atexit. Read in full; the many individual default fields were not each named. Confirmed initialization of ramp records at voice offsets 0x36c, 0x37c, 0x38c, 0x39c and 0x3ac to 30-tick reload lengths (words at 0x378/0x388/0x398/0x3a8/0x3b8 = 0x001e0000). Also word at voice+0x4bc = 0x00640000 (100-tick reload for record at +0x4b0) and at voice+0x4dc = 0x001e0000 (30-tick reload for record at +0x4d0). Round 104 cross-reference to Voice__render identifies the seven DSP ramp records as osc1 wavetable position +0x36c (30 ticks), osc2 wavetable position +0x37c (30), osc1 level +0x38c (30), osc2 level +0x39c (30), noise level +0x3ac (30), filter cutoff +0x4b0 (100), and voice volume +0x4d0 (30). This identifies their consumers, not all possible later reload overrides. The separate pan record +0x4e0 is set directly at Voice__trigger and must not be folded into the seven reload defaults.

name: Timbre__deletingDtor
description: Deleting destructor (vtable 0x3c07114c): calls operator delete(this, 0x4074); 0x4074 is the size printed by the console for sizeof(SynthTimbre).

name: Lfo__updateGlobal
description: Same algorithm as Lfo__update (byte-for-byte copy with the sine table at 0x3c071160), used for the shared LFOs at shared object +0x4030 and +0x404c from VoiceEngine__controlTick. Fields and shapes as in Lfo__update. Read in full.

name: WavetableCache__init
description: WavetableCache__init (shared DSP object a2) uses global cache pointer 0x3fcbdcc0. On first call allocates 0x58c83 bytes using heap-caps flag 0x400, aligns returned pointer to even, stores it globally, initializes header u16 values 100 and 0; zeroes the 89*61*64 wave bytes, 89*61 flag bytes, 24*61 u16 user table map, 24-byte region at +0x56dea, and 122*64 user pool, then calls WavetableCache__buildAll 0x4202c500. Allocation failure logs two messages and does not produce a valid cache. On every call writes cache pointer to shared DSP +20 and +0x201c, clears +24 and +0x2020, and constructs two identical 64x128 signed-byte scratch tables at +28 and +0x2024. Rows 0..60 use table 0 waves; rows 61..63 use table 88 waves 0..2. Samples 0..63 are unsigned wave bytes minus 128; samples 64..127 are reverse-order 127 minus original byte. The previously undecoded SALT (0x4201693c/0x420169bc) selects table 88 precisely when row index >60. The two 8 KB banks are live, per-shared-engine, table-indexed decoded-wave caches, not unreferenced buffers: Voice__render reads their 128-byte rows through descriptor pointers installed by Voice__init. Each descriptor consists of cache-base pointer at +0, selected table number at +4, and a 64 by 128 signed-byte bank starting +8. A table change in Voice__render rebuilds the corresponding bank. The first header u16 is initialized to 100 here, but code-built table 69 (HeavyFuz) overwrites and subsequently reads it as its mutable 16-bit feedback/LFSR state in WavetableCache__buildSynthTables. In that builder, 200 is the local initial feedback seed. Therefore the field's use is verified, but any special meaning for the original initialization literal 100 remains unverified. The separate 24-byte zeroed area at cache+0x56dea has no verified semantic reader or later writer. Round 105: On successful first cache allocation, buildAll runs before return. Header word 100 is overwritten in the HeavyFuz builder by a local-seed-200 feedback state before its first identified feedback read. The cache+0x56dea area is a separate 12-u16 zeroing loop, outside the 24x61-u16 user map and user-wave pool; no later direct semantic reader is verified.

name: VoiceEngine__init
description: Init of a shared DSP object (a2; a3 byte stored at +4, a4 at +8, a5 at +12 = the per-part float array pointer used by VoiceEngine__controlTick). Calls the wave cache preparation 0x4201682c with a2 and the NoteProcessor instance accessor 0x4201467c, then sets +0x4068 = note processor + 16 (the tempo clock record), clears the shared LFO 1 fields (+0x4030 word, s16 +0x4034, retrigger byte +0x4036 = 1) and the LFO 2 fields (+0x404c word, s16 +0x4050, byte +0x4052 = 1). Read in full.

name: PartArray__at
description: Returns the address of part i: 0x3fcbdcc4 + i x 0x4074 (stride 0x4074 per part object). Called from fcn.42014a6f. Read from the code.

name: VoiceEngine__ctor
description: Static constructor of the four shared DSP objects (base 0x3fcbdcc4, stride 0x4074, end 0x3fccde94). For each: vtable 0x3c071148, bytes and words at +4..+24 cleared, 2048 words cleared at +28 and 2048 words at +0x2024 (wave copy buffers), +0x201c and +0x2020 cleared; the control tick fields at +0x4024..: position 0, deadline 49, tick count 0, several fields cleared, and the LFO skew floats at +0x4040 and +0x405c set to 0.5. Finally registers the destructor 0x4204e8b0 with __cxa_atexit. Read in full. The two preexpanded 8 KB banks are consumed through oscillator descriptor pointers by Voice__render and are repopulated on wavetable-table changes, as shown in Round 102; they are not unused scratch allocations.

name: Format__BPM
description: BPM formatter (vt 0x3c072010): converts the 0..1 value to a double, multiplies by 380.0 and adds 20.0, prints it with "%.0f" into a 64-byte buffer and copies the text to the caller's buffer (size a3). So BPM = 20 + 380 x, 20..400; this agrees with the BPM default 0.263158 = 100/380 in PARAMS.md (120 BPM).

name: TempoClock__initState
description: Initialises the first 16 bytes of the TempoClock (note processor obj+0x10): [0] float 0.2632 (0x3e86bca2, the BPM parameter x; 20 + 380 x = 120.0), [4] float 1.0 (the enabled switch tested as above 0.1 by TempoClock__update and the rhythm clock reset), [8..15] the double 120.0 (low word 0, high word 0x405e0000, the BPM double at +8/+12). Called from the static initialiser at 0x42014694 (the one that builds the layer voice managers), which passes the object at 0x3fca5838. Read from the code.

name: TempoClock__init
description: Init of the internal tempo clock object (note processor obj+0x10). Reads the float x at +0, converts to double and sets bpm = 20 + 380 x at +8 and +16, samples per beat = 2,646,000 / bpm (the constant 0x41442ff8 is the high word of the double 2,646,000.0 = 44100 x 60) at +24, clears byte +32, +40/+44 and +48/+52 (beat position), +64 = 0 and +68 = 0x40e58880 (together the double 44100.0, the sample rate), byte +80 and +88/+92 = double -1.0 (last Song Position handled). Corrected in Round 50: the earlier 2.5e6 and 7.17 readings were wrong.

name: TempoClock__update
description: Per-block tempo clock update (a2 = TempoClock, a3 = copy of the transport record at note processor obj+0x70; the float at +4 is the enabled switch, the byte at +32 is the sync-BPM-in-use flag). Previous BPM +16/+20 = +8/+12. If float +4 is above 0.1 and record byte +1 is set, BPM +8/+12 = record double at +8 (when the sync flag was clear it logs Time::update: Switch to sync bpm); otherwise BPM = 20 + 380 x (x = float at +0) and, if the sync flag was set, it logs Switch to internal bpm; the sync flag is set or cleared accordingly. Samples per beat +24/+28 = 44100.0 (double +64/+68) x 60 / BPM, every block. When +4 is above 0.1: with a valid Song Position (record byte +32, double +40) that differs from the last handled one (+88/+92) or while +80 is clear, the beat position +48/+52 and the chase target +56/+60 become ceil(position) + frac(SPP), the offset +72/+76 = new position - SPP, +80 = 1, +88/+92 = SPP and a log line is written; otherwise, with +80 set and record bytes +0 and +16 set, target = record beat position (double +24) + offset and position += 0.04 x (target - position) per block; with +80 set and either record byte clear, +80 is cleared. Not run. Re-read against the disassembly; the round 50 text stands, except that the byte at +32 is a sync-BPM-in-use flag, not a tempo-changed flag.

name: TempoClock__advance
description: TempoClock__advance (clock a2, unsigned 64-bit sample increment a4 low/a5 high, normally 16/0). Updates u64 sample count at +40/+44: low'=low+a4, carry=(low'<old_low) unsigned by SALTU encoding 0x62cdc0, high'=old_high+a5+carry. Converts unsigned 64-bit increment to double (__floatundidf), adds increment/rate to double beat-position accumulator at +48/+52 (__divdf3 and __adddf3). The rate is the double samples-per-beat at +24/+28 if it exceeds 5.0, otherwise the fallback double 60.0. TempoClock__init at 0x42016b40 sets samples-per-beat=2646000/BPM (44100*60/BPM), and initializes the +48 accumulator to zero, independently confirming its unit is beats. No sound processing or hardware behavior asserted.

name: ChordTable__staticInit
description: Static init (vt 0x3c082e24): fills the chord table at 0x3fcce170 (17 entries, 36 bytes each: up to 4 semitone offsets then the count at +32) and the scale-degree table at 0x3fcce098 (6 entries, same layout). Chord entries (checked by replaying the stores): 0 {0,4,7}, 1 {0,3,7}, 2 {0,5,7}, 3 {0,3,6}, 4 {0,4,8}, 5 {0,5,10}, 6 {0,4,7,11}, 7 {0,3,7,10}, 8 {0,4,7,10}, 9 {0,5,7,10}, 10 {0,4,7,9}, 11 {0,3,6,10}, 12 {0,3,6,9}, 13 {0,4,8,10}, 14 {0,4,8,11}, 15 {0,4,6,10}, 16 {0,3,7,11}. Scale-degree entries (steps counted along the active scale): 0 {0,2,4}, 1 {0,2,4,6}, 2 {0,3,4}, 3 {0,3,4,6}, 4 {0,4,8}, 5 {0,2,4,6,8}. Chord names (major, minor, sus4, diminished, augmented and so on) are only inferred from the intervals.

Random value generator (vt 0x3c071a70): ROM rand (0x400014a0); first value n mod 10001 x 1e-4 (0 to 1) stored as float at this+12; second value m mod 20001 x 1e-4 - 1.0 (-1 to +1) stored as float at this+16; then clears 27 records (8-byte stride) from this+0x12c. Corrected from the code: the second range is -1..+1, not 'mod about 2.6k'.
deleting destructor: operator delete(this, 0x248); class size 0x248, trivial member destruction

name: ModMatrix__ctor
description: Constructor of the ModMatrix class (vtable 0x3c071a68, 0x248 bytes, built in place at voice+0x5e0; the destination and source name lists at 0x3c071a74 and 0x3c071ae0 sit right behind its vtable). +4 = 0, +8 = 1.0 (source Constant), +12 = 0 (source Random, redrawn by the virtual method fcn.42016fcc), +16 = 0 (source Rand Bipol). A table of 35 source records {float pointer, flag byte} from +0x14, one per ModmatSrc choice, zeroed except Off (record 0, points to this+4), Random (32, this+12), Rand Bipol (33, this+16) and Constant (34, this+8); the other records are bound by Voice__init. A table of 27 destination records {word, flag byte, u16} from +0x12c, zeroed; 16 words from +0x204 and u16 +0x244 zeroed. Ends by calling fcn.42016fcc. Replaces the earlier name RandomSource__ctor.

name: HeldKeys__nextByPressTime
description: Successor of note a3 in press order: among held notes returns the one whose (64-bit press time, note number) pair is the smallest above that of a3 (equal times order by note number); -1 if a3 is above 127, nothing is held, or no later note exists (no wrap-around).

name: HeldKeys__nextByVelocityUp
description: Held note with the closest velocity above that of note a3 (strict float compare, the best value is tracked as a truncated 16-bit integer, start bound 32767); equal velocities are ordered by note number, only higher notes than a3 qualify at equal velocity, and among equal candidates the lowest note wins; -1 if a3 is above 127, nothing held or no such note (no wrap-around).

name: HeldKeys__nextByVelocityDown
description: Mirror of HeldKeys__nextByVelocityUp: the held note with the closest velocity below that of note a3 (start bound -1.0); at equal velocity only lower notes than a3 qualify and among equal candidates the highest note wins; -1 if none.

name: ScaleMask__build
description: Builds the scale mask object (this, a3 = scale type, a4 = root 0 to 11; the one instance sits at sequencer object + 0x29c and is filled by Arp__updateScaleMask). Stores the root pitch class (root + 12) mod 12 at this+96 and the number of set flags at this+100. Writes 12 records of 8 bytes at this+0: byte flag (1 when the pitch class is in the scale) and a word at +4 (pointer to the note name string). The flag of record i is the mask byte [scale x 12 + ((i - root) mod 12)] of the byte table at 0x3c071e0c (24 scales x 12 bytes, written relative to the scale's own root, so the mask is rotated by the root). Name row: a table of 12 rows x 12 string pointers at 0x3c071bcc (row stride 48 bytes) holds the note spellings (row 0 C C# D Eb E F F# G G# A Bb B, row 1 C Db D Eb Fb F Gb G Ab A Bb Cb, row 6 B# C# Cx D# E E# F# Fx G# A A# B). Row choice: scale 1 (Whole Tone) row 0 for an even root and row 3 for an odd root; scales 0 and 2 row 0; every other scale row (root + 12 - offset[scale]) mod 12 with the offset taken from the word table at 0x3c071b6c (0,0,0,0,9,0,9,2,4,5,7,11,0,9,10,7,7,6,11,7,0,0,10,9); a scale type above 23 is treated as 23 with offset 9. Read in full from the code. Not checked: which names appear for which key beyond the row selection.
returns pointer/constant 0x7fffffff

name: Default__outParams
description: Writes 0 to the word out parameter a6, 0 to the byte out parameter a7 and 1.0 (0x3f800000) to the float whose pointer is on the stack (default-value accessor).
deleting destructor: operator delete(this, 8); class size 8, trivial member destruction

name: ParamMgr__ctor
description: Constructor of the note and parameter processor (vtable 0x3c071f34 at +12, words +0, +4, +8 = 0). Builds the arp generator with fcn.42017e28 at this+20, the chord and scale object with fcn.42018418 at this+84, sets word +0x364 = 0, builds the clock with fcn.42017e50 at this+0x368 (earlier text gave the arp offset as 0x744, which is not what the code passes). Then zeroes fields at this+0x13d0 (byte +0, words +4, +8, +12, +16, byte +20, words +24, +28, +80, +84, +88) and at this+0x142c, +0x1430, +0x1434 and byte +0x14b8.

name: ArpSink__noteOn
description: Sends one note-on from the arp or sequencer runner to the sink. Args: this = arp object A (A+0 timing owner, A+4 held-key object, A+8 sink), a3 note, a4 previous-note value (only passed on), a5 octave offset (not used), a6 float velocity. Folds the note into 0 to 127 in steps of 12. Calls slot +12 of the sink (NoteProcessor__noteOnFloat_secondary: sink, note, a4, velocity, channel) with the channel taken from the signed byte at held-key object +0x680 (obj+0x720, the byte NoteProcessor__noteOff writes) and the two timing words of the owner (*(A)+40 and +44) as extra stack arguments that the float overload does not use. If the byte A+0x1436 is non-zero, writes the 16-bit value 0x100 there, which clears byte +0x1436 and sets byte +0x1437 to 1 (meaning of +0x1437 not established). Then writes 100 to the sounding-notes table at A+0x1438+note. Read in full.

name: ArpSink__noteOff
description: Sends one note-off from the arp or sequencer runner to the sink. Args: this = arp object A, a3 note (a4 is not used). Folds the note into 0 to 127 in steps of 12. Calls slot +16 of the sink (NoteProcessor__noteOffFloat_secondary: sink, note, velocity 0.0, channel) with the channel taken from the signed byte at held-key object +0x680 (obj+0x720) and the owner timing words *(A)+40 and +44 as the fifth and sixth arguments (the float overload does not use them). Then writes 2 to the sounding-notes table at A+0x1438+note (note-on writes 100 there). Read in full.

name: ArpSeq__stop
description: Arp/seq stop (called when the ArpSeqMode parameter goes to Off): clears the 16-bit flag at obj+0x1434 (byte +0x1434 enabled and byte +0x1435 runner active both cleared), stops the runner at obj+0x13d0 (fcn.4201883c), sends an all-notes-off through slot +8 of the voice owner (obj+8) with the two words at *(obj)+40/+44, re-initialises the note slot table at obj+0x13d0 (fcn.4204eda0) and clears the 128 bytes at obj+0x1438 (table of notes the arp has sounded). Decoded from aligned code.

name: ArpSeq__checkHeldStart
description: Per-tick check of the held table: scans 32 words (the 128 held flags at obj+0xa0, reached through the pointer at this+4). If any word is non-zero and the runner-active byte obj+0x1435 is 0, it sets that byte to 1, starts the runner at obj+0x13d0 with fcn.42018810 and sets byte obj+0x1436 to 1. If all 32 words are zero and the runner-active byte is set, it clears that byte, stops the runner (fcn.4201883c), sends an all-notes-off through slot +8 of the voice owner (words at *(this)+40/+44) and re-initialises the note slot table with fcn.4204eda0. So the arp stops by itself as soon as the held table is empty; a latch that keeps the held flags set would keep it running. Decoded from aligned code (the stop path needed the branch-target decode).

name: ArpSeq__bindMode
description: Mode rebinding: stores the requested mode word at obj+0x142c into the applied mode word at obj+0x1430 (reads it as old value at +0x1430); when it changed, or a3 is non-zero, binds the runner (obj+0x13d0) to the generator config of the new mode with fcn.4204ed80: mode 1 uses obj+20, mode 2 uses obj+84, mode 0 uses obj+12, each with the output table obj+0x368. Other values do nothing.

name: ArpSeq__start
description: Arp/seq start (called when the ArpSeqMode parameter leaves Off): sets the 16-bit flag at obj+0x1434 to 1, calls ArpSeq__bindMode(obj, 0), then for arp and seq modes (mode word at obj+0x1430 minus 1 is below 2) calls ArpSeq__checkHeldStart (starts the runner only when keys are held); for other mode values sets byte obj+0x1435 to 1 and starts the runner with fcn.42018810.

name: ArpSeq__tick
description: Per-block tick of the arp and sequencer (A = obj+0x728, called from the note processor block tick fcn.42013e30). (1) Calls ArpSeq__bindMode(A, 0); the result is non-zero when the requested mode word (+0x142c) differs from the applied one (+0x1430). (2) If the mode changed while the arp is enabled (byte +0x1434): stops the runner (ArpRunner__stop on A+0x13d0), sends all-notes-off through sink slot +8 with the owner timing words and re-initialises the note slot table (HeldTable__init); if it changed while disabled, a set flag +0x14b8 is cleared and the function returns. (3) Flag byte +0x14b8: when set it is simply cleared (no scan); when clear the 32 held-flag words (pointer at A+4) are scanned and, if none is set, the flag is set to 1 and the 128-byte sounding table at +0x1438 is cleared. So while no key is held the flag alternates every tick and the table is cleared on every second tick. (4) Only when enabled: for applied mode 1 or 2 and a non-zero new-key byte at held-key object +0x681 (obj+0x721) it calls ArpSeq__checkHeldStart. (5) If the runner-active byte +0x1435 is set it calls ArpRunner__step on A+0x13d0. Read in full. Not checked: who clears the new-key byte +0x681.

name: ArpSeq__setup
description: Setup of the arp object A (args: A = obj+0x728, a3 = timing owner = TempoClock at obj+0x10, a4 = held-key object obj+0xa0, a5 = sink obj+4). Stores them at A+0, A+4 and A+8. Then: arp generator init (fcn.4204ecf8 on A+0x14: held-key pointer at gen+4 and gen+44, helper cursor gen+52 = 60); sequencer attach (fcn.4204ed40 on A+0x54: held-key pointer at seq+8); the SeqLen modulation pointer A+0x2e8 = A+0x364 (a float that nothing writes, so it stays 0); RhythmClock__initPatterns on the rhythm clock A+0x368 with the owner A[0]; NoteSlots__init on the runner A+0x13d0 (a3 = A, a4 = A[0]); finally ArpSeq__bindMode(A, 1), which forces the generator binding. Read in full.

name: ParamFormat__percent
description: ParamInfo formatter (buf, size, float): value x 100 converted to a double and printed with the format "%.0f%%" (string at 0x3c0652f4) through the snprintf-like fcn.4204090c. Older notes say this is the formatter of AmpEnvVelocity (not re-checked here). Read in full.

name: ParamFormat__seqPitch
description: ParamInfo formatter (signature buf, size, float): converts the float to double, adds 0.05, truncates to int n and prints snprintf(buf, size, "%+d", n - 48). Held in the formatter slot (record +28) of the descriptor table entry that precedes SeqStep1Velo, that is SeqStep1Pitch (97 steps, default 48.0 = +0); no other table slot holds it. Read from the code.

name: ParamFormat__plusOne
description: ParamInfo formatter (buf, size, float): rounds as ParamFormat__seqPitch (+0.05 in double, truncated) and prints "%d" of n + 1. Held in the formatter slots of RhythmPattern (16 steps) and SeqLen (32 steps, default 15 so 16 is shown). Read from the code.

name: ParamFormat__wavetableName
description: ParamInfo formatter for the 64-step wavetable parameter (buf, size, float step). n = trunc(step + 1e-4); table number = n for n up to 31, else n + 24. For table numbers 0 to 87 it prints "%d %s" (format at 0x3c065304) with n + 1 and the 8-character name from the pointer array at 0x3fca05ac (88 entries: 0 to 31 factory, 32 to 55 User 1 to User 24, 56 to 87 factory); otherwise "%d unknown" (0x3c06530c). So knob steps 32 to 63 are shown as tables 56 to 87 and the 24 User tables are skipped. Display only; whether the engine uses the same mapping is not traced here. Read in full.
deleting destructor: operator delete(this, 64); class size 64, trivial member destruction
vt 0x3c072d44: reset, sets this+0x38 = -1 and this+0x28 = 0 inline, or calls the override when slot +0xc is not the default fcn.4204ed08

name: ParamFormat__octaves
description: ParamInfo formatter (buf, size, float): rounds as ParamFormat__seqPitch and prints "%d Oct" of n + 1. Held in the formatter slot of ArpOctaves (4 steps, default 2 so 3 Oct is shown). Read from the code.

name: HeldKeys__firstNote_forward
description: Start-of-sweep picker for the upward direction. this+0 = held-key object, this+4 = note order mode word, result stored at this+8 and returned (note or -1). Mode 0 oldest key (fcn.4204e9c8), 1 newest (4204ea4c), 2 lowest note (4204e960), 3 highest note (4204e990), 4 lowest velocity (4204ebd8), 5 highest velocity (4204ec4c), 6 same as 0, other values return the stored this+8 unchanged. HeldKeys__firstNote (0x4201799c) is the mirrored picker for the downward direction. Whole function read.

name: HeldKeys__nextNote_forward
description: Next-note selector over the held-key set, switch on the mode word at this+4 (this+0 = held-key object, this+8 = current note, result stored back to this+8): 0 = fcn.420170dc (next by press time, later), 1 = fcn.4204ead0 (by press time, other direction), 2 = fcn.4204e918 (next higher note number), 3 = fcn.4204e93c (next lower note number), 4 = fcn.420171bc (by velocity, one direction), 5 = fcn.4201728c (by velocity, other direction), 6 = reset current note to -1, anything else returns the current note unchanged. Switch confirmed from the code. Held-key object: bytes 0..127 are the held flags, 64-bit press times at +0x280. Which arp mode number drives which case was not traced.

name: HeldKeys__firstNote
description: Picks the starting note by the mode word at this+4 over the held-key object this+0 and stores it at this+8: 0 = newest pressed (fcn.4204ea4c), 1 = oldest pressed (fcn.4204e9c8), 2 = highest note (fcn.4204e990), 3 = lowest note (fcn.4204e960), 4 = highest velocity (fcn.4204ec4c), 5 = lowest velocity (fcn.4204ebd8), 6 = same as 0 (newest; the earlier text saying reset to -1 was wrong, only the next-note selectors reset on 6), other values return the stored note unchanged. Returns the note or -1. Whole function read.

name: HeldKeys__nextNote_backward
description: Next-note selector for the downward direction, mode word at this+4 (forward selector HeldKeys__nextNote_forward has the pairs swapped): 0 = predecessor by press time (fcn.4204ead0), 1 = successor by press time (fcn.420170dc), 2 = next lower note (fcn.4204e93c), 3 = next higher note (fcn.4204e918), 4 = next lower velocity (fcn.4201728c), 5 = next higher velocity (fcn.420171bc), 6 = reset to -1, other values return the stored note; result stored at this+8. Whole function read.

name: ArpGen__randomHeldNote
description: Random held note for the arp algorithm Random (this = collection object at generator+44, this+0 = held-key object). r = ROM rand (0x400014a0) mod 20. Starts at the lowest held note (fcn.4204e960, returns -1 when nothing is held) and moves up r times to the next held note (fcn.4204e918), wrapping to the lowest held note when no higher one exists; returns that note. At most 19 steps, so the pick is uniform only when the number of held notes divides 20. Read in full.

name: ArpGen__step
description: Arp generator step (slot +24 of vtable 0x3c072d34). Args: this = generator at A+0x14 (obj+0x73c), a3 = out notes int[4], a4 = out octave offsets int[4], a5 = out velocities float[4], a6 = out count, a7 = out tie byte, stack argument = out gate float. Fields: +4 and +44 held-key object (the object at +44 is handed to the HeldKeys helpers, whose mode word is at +48 and cursor at +52), +8 note order float (2.0), +12 ArpReset value, +16 reset-pending byte, +20 velocity-source float, +24 applied algorithm, +28 ArpAlgo, +32 reset limit, +36 octave count, +40 octave counter, +56 current note (-1 = none), +60 direction (0 up, 1 down). Flow: (1) if the pending byte is set, +32 = ArpReset + 1 when ArpReset >= 1 else 0x7fffffff, byte cleared. (2) Writes tie byte 0 and gate 1.0. (3) No held key (all 32 flag words zero): count 0 and return. (4) If ArpAlgo differs from the applied algorithm it is stored and the state is reset (note -1, octave counter 0). (5) Order mode = int(float +8 + 0.05) stored at +48. (6) Algorithm 6 Random: note = ArpGen__randomHeldNote, octave counter = rand() mod octave count. Otherwise, with no current note: algorithms 0, 2, 3 start with HeldKeys__firstNote_forward, direction up, octave 0; algorithms 1, 4, 5 start with HeldKeys__firstNote, direction down, octave = count - 1. With a current note and direction up: next = HeldKeys__nextNote_forward; at the end of the held notes the octave counter goes up and the sweep restarts at the first note until the top octave; there algorithm 0 wraps to octave 0, algorithms 2 and 4 take the last note then one step down and turn down (end note not repeated; a single held key just holds), algorithms 3 and 5 repeat the end note and turn down. Direction down is the mirror (nextNote_backward; at the bottom the octave counter goes down; at octave 0 algorithm 1 wraps to the top octave and last note, algorithms 2 and 4 take the first note then one step up and turn up, algorithms 3 and 5 repeat the first note and turn up). (7) Output: for order mode other than 6 one note = current note + 12 x octave counter (folded down by 12 while above 127), count 1. Mode 6 (a chord, unreachable while the order float stays 2.0) outputs the lowest-velocity held note plus up to three higher held notes, each plus 12 x octave counter. (8) Velocity: int(float +20 + 0.05) = 1 takes the velocity of the oldest held key, 2 of the newest, anything else the velocity of the current note (0 if invalid), copied to all outputs; octave offsets = 12 x octave counter. Nothing was found that writes the floats at +8 and +20 (they keep 2.0 and 0, so the order is ascending note number and the velocity comes from the current note); unconfirmed.

name: ArpGen__ctor
description: Constructor of the arp generator (64 bytes, vtable 0x3c072d34, built in place at A+0x14 = obj+0x73c). Sets +0 vtable, +8 float 2.0 (note order), +12 = 0 (ArpReset value), +16 byte 0 (reset pending), +20 = 0 (velocity-source float), +24 = 0 (applied algorithm), +28 = 0 (ArpAlgo), +32 = 0x7fffffff (no reset limit), +36 = 3 (octave count). Other fields come from the attach slot (fcn.4204ecf8: +4 and +44 = held-key object, +52 = 60) and the reset slot (+56 = -1, +40 = 0); +48 and +60 are not initialised here. Read in full.

name: RhythmClock__init
