description: Init of the rhythm clock object (a sub-object of ParamMgr). Fields set: +40/+44 = 0 (word pair), +48 byte = 0 (step active), +52 float 0.5 (gate, relative; plain half), +56 float 10.0 (step length index 10 = the 0.25 beat entry, a 16th note), +60 float 0.5 (swing amount, 0.5 = straight), +64 float 1.0, +68 int 0 (rhythm pattern index), +72/+76 pointers 0 (modulation inputs for gate and swing), +80/+84 double 1.0 (step length ratio). From +92 a table of 16 rhythm patterns, each 32 steps of 8 bytes {u8 = 1, float 1.0}, 0x100 bytes per pattern (end at +0x105c). At +0x1000+92 the current pattern (0), at +0x1000+96 the pattern length 32.

name: RhythmClock__initPatterns
description: Fills the 15 predefined rhythm patterns (patterns 1 to 15; pattern 0 stays all on) into the table at this+0x15c: a pattern's step byte is 1 where the matching word of the 16-step source table at 0x3c072d54 (64 bytes per pattern) is non-zero, else 0; the 16 source steps repeat for the 32 steps. Stores a3 at this+0. Source patterns, 16 steps (x = on): 1 x.xxx.xxx.xxx.xx, 2 x.x.x..xx.x.x..x, 3 x.x.x.xxx.x.x.xx, 4 x.xxx.x.x.xxx.x., 5 x.x.xx.xx.x.xx.x, 6 xx.x.xx.xx.x.xx., 7 x.x.x.x.xx.x.x.x, 8 x.x.x.xx.x.xx.x., 9 xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx., 10 xx.xx.xx.xx.xxx., 11 xx.xx.xx.xx.x.x., 12 xx.xx.x.xx.xx.x., 13 x.x.x.x.xx.x.xxx, 14 x..x..x..x..x..x, 15 x.x.x.x.x..xx.x.

name: RhythmClock__resync
description: Same time alignment as RhythmClock__reset (0x42017f78) - copies owner +48/+52 to +40 and +8, the lock byte (owner+80, or 0 when owner float +4 is not above 0.1) to +49, applies ceilf(position - 0.042) when owner+4, owner+80 and the clock float +64 allow it, and sets the gate-off times +16/+24 to 1e100 - but it does not clear +88, the step index (+0x1064) or byte +48, so the step counter keeps running. Its only caller is RhythmClock__loadStepLength (0x42018098), which calls it when the cached lock byte +49 differs from the current lock state (owner+80 when owner float +4 is above 0.1, else 0). Read from the code.

name: RhythmClock__reset
description: Start or reset of the clock: copies owner +48/+52 (beat position) to +40 and +8, copies owner byte +80 (locked) to +49. When the float at owner+4 is above 0.1, owner+80 is set and the clock float at +64 is above 0.1, the first step time +8 becomes ceilf(position - 0.042) as a double (next whole beat with 0.042 beats of grace). Then sets +16/+24 to the double 0x54b249ad2594c37d (1e100 = no gate-off pending), +88 = 0 and the step index at +0x1000+100 = 0, byte +48 = 0. (0.042 corrected from 0.0442 in Round 50.)

name: RhythmClock__swingStepLength
description: Step length of the next step (a2 = clock; returns a double in a2:a3). x = float at this+60 (swing) plus the float behind the pointer at this+76 (0 when the pointer is null). s = 0.05 when x < 0, 0.95 when x > 1, else 0.05 + 0.9 x. Result = double at this+80/+84 (base step length from the step length table) x 2s when bit 0 of the step counter at this+88 is clear (even steps), or x 2 (1 - s) when it is set (odd steps). This confirms the earlier claim about even and odd steps; the parity is bit 0 of +88, which RhythmClock__advance increments after each step. Called from RhythmClock__advance. Read from the code.

name: RhythmClock__loadStepLength
description: Rounds the StepLen float at this+56 (value + 0.05, truncated) and limits it to 0..16, loads the double at 0x3c073118 + 8 x index into this+80/+84 (table: 4, 3, 2, 1.5, 1, 0.75, 2/3, 0.5, 0.375, 1/3, 0.25, 0.1875, 1/6, 0.125, 0.09375, 1/12, 0.0625), limits the pattern index at this+68 to 0..15 and stores it at this+0x1000+92, then reads the velocity-like float at owner+4 (unused in the part read). Index 10 (default) gives 0.25.

name: RhythmClock__advance
description: Per-step clock advance, args (this, float* out): takes the clock time (owner+48/+52, a double), rounds it through a float (truncdfsf2 then extendsfdf2), and compares it (ROM double compare 0x40002388) with the next step time at this+8/+12; returns 0 if not yet due. When due: stores the step time in +24/+28; computes the gate-off time inline (same arithmetic as RhythmClock__setGateOff with weight 1: gate = float this+52 plus the float behind the pointer at this+72, clamped to 0..1, times the step length at +32/+36, plus the step time) into +16/+20; gets the next step length from RhythmClock__swingStepLength into +32/+36; next step time +8/+12 = step time + new length; looks up the pattern byte at this + 92 + 8 x (pattern x 32 + step index) with pattern = word at this+0x1000+92 and step index = word at this+0x1000+100; sets the active byte +48 to 1 only when that pattern byte equals 1 (0 and 2 give 0); writes the float at entry offset +96 to *out; increments the step counter at +88; advances the step index modulo the pattern length (word at this+0x1000+96) and stores it. Returns the active byte (1 only when the pattern byte was 1). Checked against the disassembly.

name: RhythmClock__setGateOff
description: Sets the gate-off time at this+16/+20: gate g = float at this+52 plus the float behind the pointer at this+72 (0 if none); g below 0 gives 0 (the weight becomes 0), g above 1 uses the double argument a4:a5 (the step weighting) alone, otherwise the weight is g x a4:a5. Gate-off time = last step time (+24/+28) + weight x step length (+32/+36). Checked against the disassembly.

name: RhythmClock__gateOffDue
description: Tests whether the gate-off time at this+16/+20 has passed (clock time owner+48/+52 rounded through a float, then compared as a double). Returns 0 if not due. When due it resets the gate-off time to 1e100 (0x54b249ad2594c37d) and returns (active byte +48) AND (pattern byte of the step index now stored at this+0x1000+100 is not 2). Because RhythmClock__advance has already incremented that index, this is the byte of the NEXT step: a tie (2) in the next step suppresses the gate-off, so the note is held into that step. Checked against the disassembly.
deleting destructor: operator delete(this, 0x310); class size 0x310, trivial member destruction

name: Sequencer__reset
description: Slot +12 of the sequencer vtable 0x3c0731a8, called by Sequencer__start. Clears the direction byte +0x29b, then by SeqReset (byte +0x290): 0 Start sets the position byte +0x299 to 0 for SeqDir 0 and 2 to 5, to the last step for SeqDir 1 (backward: n - 1 with n = clamp(SeqLen + 1 + int(31 x modulation + 0.05), 1, 32)) and leaves it unchanged for larger SeqDir; 1 None keeps the position but turns a finished forward-once position (0xFF) into 0; 2 Random sets position = rand() mod n (C library rand, fcn.4203fe88) with n clamped to 1 to 32. For other SeqReset values the position is kept. Then copies the position to +0x298, clears the two published step floats at +0x308 and +0x30c and sets the last-base-note byte +0x29a to 0xFF so that the next step sees a new base note. The modulation float behind the pointer at +0x294 stays 0, so n = SeqLen + 1. Read in full.

name: ChordScale__ctor
description: Chord and scale sub-object constructor (vtable 0x3c0731a8 at +0, +8 = 0). 32 records of 20 bytes from +0xc, each {u16 0x3000, float 0.8, float 1.0}. Word +0x28c = 0xf00, u16 +0x290 = 0, word +0x294 = 0, u16 +0x298 = 0, byte +0x29b = 0, 12 records of 8 bytes {byte, word} from +0x29c zeroed, words +0x2fc and +0x300 = 0, byte +0x304 = -1 (cached scale byte). The meaning of the 32 record block is not established.

name: Arp__updateScaleMask
description: Applies scale and root on the sequencer object (this, a2; the second argument is not used). Reads two bytes: +0x28e (scale, 24 entries: Chromatic, Whole Tone, Diminished, ... 4th + Min 2) and +0x28f (root, 13 entries: - then C to B; 0 means no root), each converted to int through a double + 0.05 which leaves the integer unchanged. Stores the flag +0x291 = (root == 0). When the scale differs from the cached signed byte at +0x304 it calls fcn.42017348(this+0x29c, scale, root) with root - 1 when the root is non-zero (C = 0), then caches the scale in +0x304. fcn.42017348 fills the scale mask object at this+0x29c: 12 records of 8 bytes (flag byte, word from table 0x3c071bcc), root mod 12 at +96 and the number of set flags at +100, using the scale tables at 0x3c071bcc and 0x3c071e0c. A root change alone does not rebuild the mask (it is passed on only at the next scale change). Which parameters those bytes hold is taken from the descriptor order (engine ids 0xc SeqScale and 0xd SeqRoot, offsets 0x282 + id); the store of the parameters into those bytes was not traced here. Called from the sequencer step function (fcn.42018640) and from Sequencer__start. Read from the code.

name: Sequencer__start
description: Slot +16 (start) of the sequencer class vtable 0x3c0731a8 (class size 0x310; the arp generator vtable 0x3c071f34 has a no-op there): calls Arp__updateScaleMask(this, 0), then calls its own vtable slot +12 (fcn.420182c8, the SeqReset handling: Start, None or Random). Called from ArpRunner__start through the generator virtual slot +0x10. Read from the code.

name: SeqStep__advancePosition
description: Sequencer step position advance (this = sequencer object at note processor obj+0x77c, byte params at +0x28c..: SeqDir +0x28c, SeqLen +0x28d, position byte +0x299, direction byte +0x29b). Step count n = (int(SeqLen + 0.05) + 1) + int(31 x modulation float behind the pointer at +0x294 + 0.05), clamped to 32; if n < 2 the position is set to 0. Then by SeqDir (int(value + 0.05)): 1 backward = (pos + n - 1) mod n; 2 ping-pong without repeating the end steps (direction byte 0 = up, turns at n-1 to n-2; going down turns at 0 to 1); 3 ping-pong with repeated end steps (turns at n-1 staying on n-1, at 0 staying on 0); 4 forward once: pos + 1 until n-1, then -1 (0xFF) and stays; anything else (0) forward = (pos + 1) mod n. Matches the manual values in NOTES.md lines 215-216. The mode 2 and 3 down-step (pos - 1 wrap) was decoded from branch targets.

name: Sequencer__step
description: Sequencer step (slot +24 of vtable 0x3c0731a8; same signature as ArpGen__step: this, out notes, out octave offsets, out velocities, out count, out tie byte, stack out gate float). Base note = newest held key (HeldKeys__newest on the held-key object at this+8). If the last-base-note byte (+0x29a) differs from the newest key it is stored and, for SeqDir 4 (forward once), the position restarts at 0; for other SeqDir the position continues. A position byte of 0xFF (finished forward-once run) or SeqDir 5 with an unchanged base note gives count 0 and gate 1.0 (no note). Otherwise +0x298 = position and the step record at this + 12 + 20 x position is read: byte +0 step type (0 note, 1 rest, 2 tie; count = 0 for type 1 else 1; tie byte = 1 for type 2), byte +1 note value (default 0x30 = 48), float +4 velocity (default 0.8), float +8 gate (1.0), floats +12 and +16 (default 0). Then Arp__updateScaleMask is called and the note value is snapped upward to the next scale pitch class: with a root set (flag +0x291 = 0) the absolute pitch (base + value) is snapped within the mask, with no root (flag set) only the value is snapped and the base note is added afterwards. The result minus 48 is folded by 12 into 0 to 127 and output as the single note with octave offset 0, velocity = float +4 and gate = float +8. The two floats +12 and +16 are published as -1 + 2 x value at this+0x308 and this+0x30c (no verified musical consumer in the traced normal sequencer path), and SeqStep__advancePosition is called. Read in full. The step type byte is never written elsewhere (all steps are notes) and SeqDir has no choice 5, so those branches are not reachable in normal use; a base note of -1 (no key) is not guarded here, the runner is stopped when no key is held.

name: ArpRunner__start
description: Starts the runner: clears the state word at +0x58, calls RhythmClock__reset (fcn.42017f78) on the clock at +0x10 when set, calls virtual slot +0x10 (start) of the generator at +0xc when set, then clears byte +0x14 and the state word +0x54 (0 = running).

name: ArpRunner__stop
description: Stops the runner: calls fcn.4204ed20 (empty clock stop hook) for the clock at +0x10 when set, calls virtual slot +0x14 (stop) of the generator at +0xc when set, sets state word +0x54 = 2 (stopped).

name: ArpRunner__step
description: Per-tick step of the runner (this = runner at A+0x13d0, called from ArpSeq__tick while A+0x1435 is set). Fields: +0 bound byte, +8 arp object A, +0xc generator (arp generator or sequencer), +0x10 rhythm clock, +0x14 tie byte (written by the generator), +0x20 list of 4 previously released notes (-1 = none, passed as the unused argument of ArpSink__noteOn), +0x30 list of 4 current notes, +0x40 list of 4 octave offsets, +0x50 count, +0x54 state (0 started, 1 notes sounding, 2 released), +0x58 step counter. Returns at once if the bound byte, the generator, the clock or A is missing. Order: (1) RhythmClock__loadStepLength. (2) If RhythmClock__gateOffDue is true, the state is 1 and the tie byte is 0: ArpSink__noteOff for each current note, copy the current notes into the +0x20 list, pad it with -1, state 2. (3) RhythmClock__advance (its out float starts at 1.0 and stays 1.0 because the per-step floats are never changed); returns when the step is not active (pattern byte 0 or 2), so the generator does not advance on rest steps. (4) Active step: notes still sounding (state 1) with the tie byte clear are released first as in (2). With the tie byte clear: generator step slot (+24) into the runner lists, then ArpSink__noteOn for each of the count notes with velocity = generator velocity x clock float, state 1. With the tie byte set (previous step was a tie): the generator is still called but into temporary lists and its notes are dropped so the sounding note keeps going; if that step has count 0 the current notes are released and state is 2. (5) The gate-off time is set with RhythmClock__setGateOff from the generator gate float (1.0 for the arp, the step gate for the sequencer). (6) The step counter is incremented; when it reaches the generator period (slot +28: ArpReset limit for the arp, 0x7fffffff for the sequencer) the generator reset slot (+12) is called, the clock step index is cleared (fcn.4204ed28) and the counter restarts at 0. Read in full. The tie paths are not reachable in normal use because no tie step type or pattern value is written.

name: ParamInfo__engineRecord
description: Record getter for a UI parameter descriptor (a2 = 28-byte descriptor from the per-layer table at 0x3fc9fb78, 84 entries, or the global table at 0x3fc9e2dc, 225 entries). If the u16 engine parameter id at descriptor+6 is at most 0x1e0 it fetches the note processor singleton (fcn.4201467c) and calls its slot +12 (engine descriptor getter fcn.42014f7c) with the signed id, returning that 32-byte engine record (may be 0). Otherwise, if the u16 effect type index at descriptor+8 is at most 74, it returns the effect parameter record 0x3c06f5c4 + 32 x index; else 0. Read in full.

name: ParamInfo__engineId
description: UI parameter index to engine parameter id (a2 = index). Index up to 0x14f: takes descriptor (index mod 84) of the table at 0x3fc9fb78 (28 bytes each), reads the s16 at +6 (negative gives -1) and returns 83 x (index / 84) + that id (layer A ids start at 149, 83 ids per layer). Index 0x150 to 0x230: returns the s16 at +6 of entry (index - 0x150) of the table at 0x3fc9e2dc unchanged (-1 when it is 0xffff). Anything above 0x230 gives -1. Used by the set-parameter event before NoteProcessor setParam (older notes). Read in full.

name: ParamDesc__globalIndex
description: Looks up the global-setting index of a parameter id (a2 = id). For ids 0..0x14f the 28-byte descriptor at 0x3fc9fb78 + 28 * id is used (entries are a 4-character tag such as "o1s_", two s16 values and an s16 at +8 that is 0xffff = -1 for these per-sound parameters); for ids 0x150..0x230 the descriptor at 0x3fc9e2dc + 28 * (id - 0x150) is used and its s16 at +8 is the sequential global-setting number (0, 1, 2, ...; entries 0 to 5 hold the tags fxt1, fxt2, bydm, chdw, chdp, chsp), ids above 0x230 return -1. Returns the s16 at descriptor +8 (sign-extended).

name: ParamInfo__tag
description: Builds the 32-bit preset tag of UI parameter index a2. Index up to 0x14f: descriptor bytes +0, +1, +2 (three name characters) as the top three bytes and the layer digit 49 + index / 84 ('1' to '4') as the low byte. Index 0x150 to 0x230: the four descriptor bytes +0 to +3 of the global table entry (index - 0x150), first byte on top. Anything above returns 0. Read in full.

name: ParamInfo__findByTag
description: Inverse of ParamInfo__tag: linear scan over the 561 UI parameter indices (0 to 0x230) comparing the tag built the same way (layer digit for the first 0x150, four bytes of the global table after that); returns the index of the first match or -1. Used by the preset loaders to match stored 4-byte tags to parameters. Read in full.

name: ParamInfo__label
description: Returns the label string (record +4) of a UI parameter. Lookup shared by all six accessors (0x42018c58, 0x42018ce0, 0x42018df8, 0x42018e80, 0x42018f08, 0x42018f9c): UI index a2 below 0x150 selects the 28-byte entry (a2 mod 84) of the per-part table at 0x3fc9fb78; indices 0x150..0x230 select entry a2 - 0x150 of the table at 0x3fc9e2dc (225 entries); other indices return a default (here the string unknown). An entry holds a 4-character tag at +0, the engine parameter id as u16 at +6 (0xffff = none), the effect type index as u16 at +8, and fallback values at +12 (label or name), +16 (default) and +20 (step count byte). If the engine id is at most 0x1e0 the record is fetched from the NoteProcessor singleton (fcn.4201467c returns 0x3fca5828) slot +12, which forwards to the engine descriptor getter (fcn.42014f7c); otherwise, if the type index is at most 74, the record is entry (type index) of the 32-byte effect parameter table at 0x3c06f5c4. If no record is found the entry fallback is returned (here the word at entry +12). Read from the code.

name: ParamInfo__name
description: Same lookup as ParamInfo__label; returns the name string (record +0), with the entry word at +12 as fallback and the string unknown for an invalid index. Read from the code.

name: ParamInfo__defaultValue
description: Default float of UI parameter index a2. Index exactly 83 (slot 'act' of layer A, Active in Multi) returns 1.0; index above 0x230 returns 0. Otherwise the descriptor is chosen as in ParamInfo__engineId and the record from ParamInfo__engineRecord supplies the default float at record+20; with no record the fallback float at descriptor+16 is returned. The older notes put the engine record default at +16; this code reads +20 (record +16 is not read here). The same slot of layers B to D (index 167, 251, 335) has no 1.0 exception and takes the record default of engine id 231 (the descriptor and its id are shared by all layers; the value was not read). Used to fill an init sound with all 561 defaults. Read in full.

name: ParamInfo__defaultValue
description: Same lookup as ParamInfo__label; returns the default float (record +16), with the entry word at +16 as fallback and 0 for an invalid index. Read from the code.

name: ParamInfo__isBipolar
description: Same lookup as ParamInfo__label; returns the byte at record +24 (the bipolar flag), or 0 when no record is found or the index is invalid. Read from the code.

name: ParamInfo__isStepped
description: Same lookup as ParamInfo__label; returns 1 when the record step count (+8) is above 0, else 0. When no record is found it returns 1 if the entry byte at +20 is non-zero, else 0; 0 for an invalid index. Read from the code.

name: ParamInfo__stepCount
description: Same lookup as ParamInfo__label; returns the record step count (+8) when it is at least 1, otherwise the entry byte at +20 (also the result when no record is found); 0 for an invalid index. Read from the code.

name: ParamInfo__formatValue
description: Generic value-to-text for UI parameter index a2 (a3 = float value, a4 = buffer, a5 = size). Descriptor and record as in ParamInfo__engineRecord. Index above 0x230 range or no descriptor: prints "%.2f". With a record whose formatter pointer (record+28) is set, calls formatter(buffer, size, value) and returns. Otherwise: if the step count (record+8, or the descriptor byte +20 when there is no record) is at least 1 it prints a label: n = trunc(value + 1e-6) limited to 0 .. steps-1; label table = record+12, else descriptor+24; prints "%s" of label[n], or "%d" of n when there is no table. Without steps: if the record's bipolar byte (record+24) is set it prints "%+.2f" of (value - 0.5) x 2, else "%.2f" of the value. Read in full.

name: InitTask__ledAnimation
description: Body of the FreeRTOS task "Init task". Copies the 10-word template at 0x3c0731c8 (values 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14) to the stack, then while the byte at 0x3fca04b8 is NON-zero (its initial value in the image is 1, and Controller__tick fcn.420196f8 clears it on every call, which ends the animation): for LED ids 0..15 calls fcn.4204f3ac(object at 0x3fcd2d78+168, id, id == template[index]) so exactly one LED is lit, increments the index modulo 10 (starting at 1), calls fcn.42028884 (the board shift-register transfer) and waits 150 ticks (FreeRTOS delay fcn.40385e4c; the tick length is not known from the binary). When the byte is zero it logs "initTask DONE!" at level 3 and deletes itself (fcn.40385cb8(0)).

name: MidiOutput__task
description: Endless MIDI output task started by the controller init. Each pass: while queue 0x3fcce43c has items it receives an 11-byte message and sends it with MidiUart__sendShort and MidiUsb__sendShort; while queue 0x3fcce438 has items it receives a block (u32 length plus data, with a selector word after the block buffer): selector 1 sends it on DIN with MidiUart__sendBlock, any other value on USB with MidiPort__sendSysexPackets; then vTaskDelay(1). Every 200 passes it calls Global__autosave(0x3fccfd14) and Sound__saveWorker(0x3fccf428). Not confirmed: which code fills queues 0x3fcce43c and 0x3fcce438.

name: Boot__showSplash
description: Boot splash routine: sets board LED brightness to 200 and forces LED id 1 on in the shift-register output, refreshes shift-register inputs, clears a 1024-byte 128x64 display buffer, constructs two font descriptors from 0x3c073b40 and 0x3c07423c and draws Protein at the top plus a horizontal line at y=22. Initializes startup state byte 0x3fccf425 to zero; sets it to 3 when button ids 13, 14 and 15 all report pressed, otherwise sets it to 1 and draws Autoplay Mode at y=32 if button id 8 is pressed, or prints and draws Version 1.03 b3 at y=32 otherwise (format arguments 1, 3, 3, using Format__snprintf). Sets display brightness index 19, flushes the 1024-byte frame, then creates Init task at 0x4201915c with stack argument 0x1000 and priority 4. Physical button labels, purpose of startup state 3 and relation of Autoplay Mode to actual playback remain unconfirmed. [Stage 16: format literal 0x420011a4 points to "Version: Bane"; splash shows that text.]

name: Controller__init
description: Controller start-up (called from App__init, 0x4200ca85). Stores a deadline at this+0x1b04 = (current time in ms) + 4000 (used by the startup demo player). Reads the first-boot flag with Storage__load(namespace "Factory", key "Data", 1 byte). When the flag is missing it puts a UI ring item {0, 0, 26, 0} into the ring 0x3fcd3298 (logs "CircularBuffer::write: is full!" if full), saves the flag (value 1), clears a 1024-byte frame buffer and draws the texts "Protein", "Init Factory" and "Presets ..." with the two font tables 0x3c073b40 and 0x3c07423c plus a horizontal line, sets display brightness 19 and sends the frame to the display. Then: Global__load on this+0x18cc; sets the param-to-CC byte table at this+0xd5c (0x231 bytes) to 0xff; restores the CC map from global settings 11..130 (cc 0..119 into the s16 table at this+0xc6c, and the reverse byte table for parameters <= 0x230); LibraryIndex__build(0x3fcd32b4); UITask__start; when this+0xfdd is not 1 it puts ring items for the first events: kind 9 {0, slot, 9, 0} when global setting 9 (last sound slot) is >= 0, else kind 8 {0, 0, 8, 0}, then kind 32 {0, 0, 32, 0}; initialises the MPE tables (note table -1, bend table 0x2000, pressure and CC 74 tables 0, flag +0xc5c = 0, any-zone byte MPE+74 = 1); creates the "Helper task" (entry MidiOutput__task 0x420191ec, core 0, priority 5, stack 0x1000, handle 0x3fcce434) and logs an error string if that fails. Not confirmed: where the factory presets are written after the first-boot flag (the factory restore code is behind controller event kind 26).

name: Controller__tick
description: Periodic controller routine (a2 = controller object; caller not identified). Clears the byte at 0x3fca04b8; pumps the message queues with fcn.4201c6c0(this+0xf8d). Pending preset change: if byte this+0x1af0 is 0 and the u16 at this+0x1af4 (pending slot) differs from the u16 at this+0x1af2: slot <= 0x167 sets the byte to 1 and writes the ring buffer entry {1, slot, 9, 0} (UI event type 9 = load slot) or logs the full buffer; a slot above 0x167 is copied into +0x1af2 and ignored. Boot demo: the state byte this+0xfdd: 1 means wait until the time (ms) reaches the due time at this+0x1b04, then DemoPlayer__start (this+0x1af8) and state 2; 2 means DemoPlayer__tick every call. Read completely.

name: CcMap__assign
description: Assigns MIDI CC a3 (0..119, else ignored) to parameter a4 (0..0x230, else ignored) on the controller a2: stores the s16 parameter index at this+0xc6c+2*cc (table at this+0xc60 plus 12), stores the cc number in the byte table at this+0xd5c+param, then calls Global__set(this+0x18cc, cc+11, param) so the mapping is persisted as global setting 11+cc. It does not clear an older CC that pointed at the same parameter or an older parameter of this CC.

name: CcMap__clear
description: Removes the mapping of MIDI CC a3 (0..119, else ignored) on the controller a2: if the old s16 parameter index at this+0xc6c+2*cc is within 0..0x230 its entry in the byte table at this+0xd5c+param is set to 0xff, then the s16 entry is set to -1 and Global__set(this+0x18cc, cc+11, -1) is called.

name: Controller__processSysexThunk
description: Thunk: calls MidiSysexController__processMessage (0x4201bbf8) with this+0x250, the two message arguments a3 and a4 passed through, and a fourth argument 1. Callers are in the output task around 0x4200cc3b and 0x4200cc60.
calls MidiSysexController__processMessage(this+0x250, message, field at this+0xfd0, 0)

name: Event__DUMP_RANGE
description: Dumps a range of sounds over SysEx (a2 = controller, a3 = first slot, a4 = last slot). Logs Event::DUMP_RANGE: slot for each, shows the text Dumping ... through UserInterface__processEvent (this+0xf8d, text copied to this+0xf8e), then for each slot from a3 to a4 loads it into a stack Sound object with fcn.42029a78 after Sound__resetEditState and, on success, calls MidiSysexController__dumpSound with port = 1 when setting 133 equals 1, else 0. After the loop waits up to 101 ticks for the SysEx queue (0x3fcce438) to drain and clears the message. Whole function read.

name: ParamEvent__push
description: Pushes one parameter to the engine and the UI (this = 0x3fcce448 controller, a3 = parameter index). Reads the value with fcn.4204f8dc(this+0xfe0, index); sends a 24-byte engine message {6, index, 0, 0, 0, value float} through Engine__sendEngineEvent (engine global 0x3fca3974); then writes a 16-byte ring buffer entry {index, trunc(value x 1e6), 7, 0} into the queue at 0x3fcd3298 (head +16, count +20, capacity +8, entries via +4), or logs CircularBuffer::write is full when count equals capacity. Type 7 is the engine-to-UI parameter update that the section handlers receive. Whole function read. The parameter value comes directly from the controller store, without re-clamping stepped values, so imported out-of-range LFO ratio floats can be forwarded unchanged to the engine.

name: Controller__handleControlChange
description: Handles one MIDI control change (a2 = controller, a3 = cc, a4 = value, a5 = part selector from the router, a6 = channel offset from the router). CC 1 also stores min(value / 127, 1.0) into parameter 0x230 of the parameter store at this+0xfe0 (mod wheel), CC 32 also stores the value in the byte at this+0x1af6 (bank LSB used by program change), CC 124 sets global setting 0 to 0 and CC 125 sets it to 1 (Global__set on this+0x18cc; roles omni off and on by value, name unconfirmed). Then, for cc <= 119 with a CC map entry (s16 at this+0xc6c+2*cc, negative means none) the value is converted and written to the parameter store, and ParamEvent__push(this, param) is called. Conversion: for parameters 0..0x14f whose index modulo 84 is 5 or 12, floor((stepCount - 1) * min(value / 127, 1)); for stepped parameters (ParamInfo__isStepped) with step count n: n < 2 gives 0, n <= 32 gives clamp((value * n) >> 7, 0, n-1), larger n gives clamp(value, 0, n-1) or, for bipolar parameters, clamp(value - 64 + (n-1)/2, 0, n-1); for continuous parameters, bipolar ones give clamp((value - 64) / 126 + 0.5, 0, 1) and others min(value / 127, 1). Last, for every cc, an engine event is sent with Engine__sendEngineEvent: {3, cc, value, a5, a6, 0}. Not confirmed: what the parameters at offsets 5 and 12 of each 84-parameter block are.

name: Controller__routeMidiMessage
description: MIDI message router (a2 = controller, a3 to a5 = the 11-byte message as three words: three MIDI bytes then an 8-byte timestamp, a6 = source flag: 0 for normal input, 2 for the startup demo player by Midi__injectNoteOff). Every message is first posted with UserInterface__processMidiInput. Status >= 0xF0 goes to MidiClock__handleSystemMessage with the timestamp from bytes 3..10. For channel messages the global setting 131 (MPE status) is read from this+0x18cc. With MPE on, setting 132 is copied to this+0xb80 and Mpe__process is called with the object at this+0xb40; a nonzero result word means the message is dropped (upper zone), otherwise the returned value becomes the part selector and the channel byte may have been rewritten. With MPE off: the part selector is -1 (accepted) when global setting 0 is nonzero, or when (channel - global setting 1) as an unsigned number is below a limit, or when a6 equals 2; otherwise the message is dropped. The limit is 4 when UI parameter 0x229 (LayerMode by earlier rounds) is 4 and parameter 0x22a is 3, else 1. Dispatch on the status high nibble: 0x80 note off event {1, note, vel, ch, 0, 0}; 0x90 note on {0, note, vel, ch, 0, 0}, with velocity 0 sent as note off {1, note, 0, ch, 0, 0}; 0xA0 {5, note, value, ch, 0, 0}; 0xB0 calls Controller__handleControlChange(cc, value, part, ch); 0xC0 program change: value = (this+0x1af6 << 7) + program, accepted when <= 0x167 and LibraryIndex__isUsed(0x3fcd32b4, value) is nonzero, then stored as s16 at this+0x1af4 (no event); 0xD0 {4, pressure, part, ch, 0, 0}; 0xE0 {2, (d2 << 7) | d1, part, ch, 0, 0}. In MPE mode a first note on (byte this+0xc5c set) additionally sends pitch bend {2, [this+0xc60], note, ch, 0, 0}, pressure {4, [this+0xc64], note, ch, 0, 0} and CC 74 {3, 74, [this+0xc68], note, ch, 0} from the three words Mpe__process copied there, and clears the byte. All events go through Engine__sendEngineEvent(0x3fca3974, 24-byte event). Not confirmed: the roles of global settings 0 and 1 (omni and base channel by use), the consumer of the program value at this+0x1af4.

name: Product__sendMidiMessage
description: Pushes a 3-byte MIDI message into the send queue (0x3fcce43c), logs "sendMidiQueue full!" when full

name: Param__sendAsCc
description: Sends one parameter value out as a MIDI control change. Arguments: this (controller object), a3 = UI parameter index (limit 0x230), a4 = float value. The CC number is the byte at this+0xd5c+index (the param-to-CC map; a negative byte means no CC and nothing is sent). Builds the 11-byte message {0xB0, cc, value, zeros} and calls Product__sendMidiMessage (channel nibble replaced there). Value 0..127: if the index (parameter number within the 84-parameter part block, index mod 84, for indices up to 0x14f) is 5 or 12 (Wtb1Pos, Wtb2Pos): trunc(x / (steps-1) * 127 + 0.5); otherwise if ParamInfo__isStepped: steps < 2 gives 0, step = trunc(x + 0.0001), with up to 32 steps value = (step*128 + 64) / steps, with more than 32 steps value = step + 64 - (steps-1)/2; else if ParamInfo__isBipolar: 64 + round-away-from-zero((x - 0.5) * 126); else trunc(x * 127 + 0.5). Always clamped to 0..127. Whole function read; the only caller found is a misattributed function bound near the boot splash, so who calls it is unconfirmed.

name: Controller__handleEvent
description: Controller event handler (a2 = controller 0x3fcce448, a3 = id, a4 = value, a5 = kind, a6 = flag). Called only from the output task 0x4200ca8c at 0x4200ccb6, which pops one 16-byte item {id, value, kind, flag} per loop from the ring buffer 0x3fcd3298 (read index +12, count +20). That ring is filled by the queue pump from the UI (queue 0x3fccff60) and by this code itself. Unless a case returns early, the original four arguments are finally forwarded to the UI through UserInterface__processEvent (queue 0x3fccff64); kinds 12, 13 and 18 only exist as these forwarded notifications. Kinds: 0 user input (only acts when this+0xfdd is 2: value 0 returns without forwarding, a nonzero value stops the demo player with Midi__injectNoteOff and clears the state); 6 set parameter id to value * 1e-6 (ParamStore__set on this+0xfe0, ParamEvent__push, then Param__sendAsCc); 8 new sound (Params__loadDefaultArray, global setting 9 = -1, push all 0x231 parameters, ring item {0, -1, 12, 0}); 9 load sound slot value (when slot <= 0x167: byte this+0x1af0 = 1, s16 this+0x1af2 = slot when id is 1, three zero 512-byte blocks to Audio__writeBlock, load the slot into the edit sound, engine event type 13, global setting 9 = slot; then push all parameters, ring item {0, slot, 12, 0} and clear this+0x1af0); 10 load sound with layer copy (slot <= 0x167: silence blocks, preset load with source layer (id >> 2) & 3 and destination layer id & 3, push all parameters, ring item {0, slot, 13, 0}); 15 save the edit sound to slot (Sound__requestSave, global setting 9 = slot); 17 delete slot (SoundLibrary__remove, ring item {0, slot, 18, 0}); 19 send the current sound as sysex (text "Dumping ..." as UI event kind 5, MidiSysexController__dumpSound on the port from global setting 133, waits up to 100 ticks for queue 0x3fcce438 to empty, clears the text); 20 Event__DUMP_RANGE (first = value, last = id); 22 send all 0x231 parameters out with Param__sendAsCc; 24 arm or clear the receive state (id 0 clear, id 1 find-free mode from slot value, id 2 overwrite mode from slot value: bytes this+0xfd4 and this+0xfdc, word this+0xfd8); 25 a received sound is complete (ring item {0, -1, 12, 0}, push all parameters, then when this+0xfd4 is set: save the edit sound in the next free slot from this+0xfd8 or, in overwrite mode, in slot this+0xfd8, advance the slot and set global setting 9); 26 restore factory presets (text "Init Presets ..." as UI event kind 5, then fcn.42029f08 on the library index, then clears the text); 32 apply global settings (display brightness setting 6, LED brightness min(setting 7 squared, 255), engine events 7, 8 and 9 with settings 4, 5 and 131, byte this+0 = (setting 10 != 0)); 34 all sound off (engine event CC 120 value 0); 35 with id 0 sets the engine gate flags through fcn.4200d4fc (value != 0). Not confirmed: the meaning of the s16 words this+0x1af2 and this+0x1af4 beyond what is written here, kind 5 as a text popup (inferred from the string argument), the layer meaning of the two 2-bit fields in the id of kind 10.

name: Product__sendMidiSysexMessage
description: Copies a sysex message into the send queue (0x3fcce438) and wakes the sender (fcn.40385e4c); logs "sendMidiSysexQueue full!" when full

name: UI__postReceiving
description: Copies a 64-byte text from a3 to ui+0xf8e (ROM memcpy) and posts UI event type 5 (info message) with UserInterface__processEvent (fcn.4201c7f8 on ui+0xf8d, arguments 0, 0, 5, payload), then delays one tick. Called from MidiSysexController__onSoundDump (the "Receiving" message). Fully read.
posts event 5 with UserInterface__processEvent(this+0xf8d, 0, 0, 5, 0), then fcn.40385e4c(1)

name: Controller__loadStreamAndPushAll
description: Takes a SysEx stream (a3 pointer, a4 length), mutes by writing a zeroed 512-byte block to the audio output (fcn.42026b28, three times), parses the stream into the sound library with fcn.42029e50 (library 0x3fcd32b4; each F0..F7 message is applied and saved), sends engine message type 13 (zeros), pushes all 0x231 (561) parameters of the controller sound (ParamEvent__push with this = 0x3fcce448), and finally writes one ring buffer entry {0, -1, 12, 0} (UI event type 12, index -1; meaning not decoded) or logs when the buffer is full. Caller not identified. Whole function read; the purpose of engine message 13 is unconfirmed.

name: Controller__initState
description: State initialisation of the controller object 0x3fcce448 (no direct caller found, probably a static initialiser; unconfirmed). Sets byte this+0 = 1; clears the 64-entry clock timestamp ring (128 words from +8) and the words +0x208, +0x210, +0x214, +0x218, +0x21c, +0x224, +0x228, +0x230, +0x234, +0x238, +0x248, +0x24c, +0x250; stores the tempo double -1.0 at +0x240 (invalid, so the first estimate falls back to 120); sets the clock-enable byte +0x220 = 1. Calls Sound__resetEditState on 0x3fcce69c and on the sound object 0x3fccf428 and Global__reset on 0x3fccfd14. MPE object: zone 1 member count +0xb80 = 15, upper zone count and enabled bytes 0, flag byte +0xc5c = 0, +0xc60 = 0x2000, +0xc64 = +0xc68 = 0, the RPN registers at +0xb8c and +0xb94 set to the two words at 0x3c0731f0 (both 0xffffffff), note table 0x3fccef88 (16 words) = -1, bend table 0x3fccefe4 (16 words) = 0x2000, the next 32 words 0. Also clears the receive state at this+0xfd0 (word), +0xfd4 (byte), +0xfd8 (word), +0xfdc (s16), sets the program words this+0x1af2 and this+0x1af4 to 255 and clears the bytes this+0x1af0 and this+0x1af6 and the word this+0x1b00. Creates the output queues 0x3fcce43c (32 items of 11 bytes: short MIDI messages) and 0x3fcce438 (4 items of 0x408 bytes: sysex blocks, 4-byte length plus up to 1024 bytes).

name: MidiSysexController__sendPresetNames
description: Reply to the preset-names request (start slot a3, count a4, port a5). Header F0 3E 2F, device id (settings value 3), 0x21, running sequence byte (counter at 0x3fccff50, 7 bit), then total message count, message number (1-based) and start slot as two 7-bit bytes. At most 31 slots per message, so ceil(count / 31) messages. Each slot is 32 bytes: 24 name characters (masked to 7 bits, zero padded), the used byte from the SoundLibrary (+24 of the entry, fcn.4204f934), 7 zero bytes; an unused slot (fcn.4204f900 returns 0) is 32 zero bytes. Then checksum (sum of bytes after F0, 7 bit) and F7; each message is sent with Product__sendMidiSysexMessage. Earlier note said the device id came from settings index 8; the code reads index 3. Fully read.

name: MidiSysexController__dumpSound
description: Sends a sound as exactly 6 SysEx messages (this, sound object a3, port a4). Header F0 3E 2F, device id (settings value 3), 0x10, sequence byte, then 6 (message count) and the message number 1-6. Message 1 also carries 2 raw bytes from sound+0x8dd and sound+0x8dc (a 16-bit field, 0x0800 after reset) and the 24-character name from sound+0x8c4 (7-bit, zero padded). Then up to 98 parameters per message, 561 in all (0x231): each is 10 bytes, the tag from fcn.42018b3c(index) and the value word from fcn.4204f8dc(sound, index), both as five 7-bit bytes. Messages 1-5 hold 98 parameters, message 6 holds 71. Checksum (sum after F0, 7 bit) and F7. First message is 1016 bytes and later full ones 990 bytes, matching the embedded factory sound data. Fully read.

name: MidiSysexController__sendResponse
description: Sends a 15-byte SysEx reply: F0 3E 2F, device id (settings value 3), 0x0F (response type), the command byte stored at this+0, the response code as two 7-bit bytes (a3, 14 bit), the 32-bit value a4 as five 7-bit bytes (bits 31-28, 27-21, 20-14, 13-7, 6-0), a checksum byte (sum of all bytes after F0, masked to 7 bits) and F7. The message is queued with Product__sendMidiSysexMessage (object 0x3fcce448) using a5 as its third argument (the output port, inferred). Logs code START and END. Codes seen from callers: 1 slot load failed, 2 wrong slot, 3 wrong checksum. Fully read.

name: MidiSysexController__dumpPreset
description: Handler for the SysEx preset dump request (this a2, slot a3, port a4). Uses a 0x910-byte Sound object on the stack: Sound__resetEditState, then fcn.42029a78(sound, slot) (loads the slot; non-zero on success, inferred); success calls MidiSysexController__dumpSound with that sound, failure calls sendResponse with code 1 and value 0. Fully read.

name: MidiSysexController__onPresetDump_1
description: Receives a sound over sysex: checks the checksum ("Wrong checksum!"), the slot ("Wrong slot %d!"), the sequence (NEW sequence started, reference id, sequence number; wrong ones are ignored and answered with sendResponse). Per message it applies parameters by tag (unknown tag is ignored) via fcn.4202944c (defaults) / fcn.420294bc (name) / fcn.42018bc4. After the last message ("ALL messages received!") it saves with fcn.42029c10 / fcn.42029dc0 ("Saving sound to slot %d")

name: MidiSysexController__onSoundDump
description: Receives the current sound over sysex into the edit buffer (0x3fccf428): shows "Receiving ..." (fcn.4201a7f8), "Off" label, checks reference id and sequence number (errors answered with sendResponse), applies parameters by tag, and on the last message logs "ALL messages received!" and finishes with fcn.4201a828 (UI event 5)

name: MidiSysexController__dumpScreen
description: Sends the 1024-byte display buffer (0x3fcd1214 to 0x3fcd1614) as 2 SysEx messages of 512 bytes each (port a3). Header F0 3E 2F, device id (settings value 3), 0x31, sequence byte, then a 2, the part number (1 or 2), then 128 little-endian 32-bit words each as five 7-bit bytes (bits 31-28 first), checksum (sum after F0, 7 bit) and F7. Fully read; the buffer start was earlier given as 0x3fcd1414 (that is the start of the second half).

name: MidiSysexController__sendFirmwareVersion
description: Builds and sends the firmware-version sysex reply (not UI code). Message: F0 3E 2F, device id (global setting 3 read with WordTable__get on 0x3fccfd14), 0x41, a sequence byte (counter at 0x3fccff50 incremented modulo 128), then 12 text bytes (7-bit masked) from snprintf "%d.%02d b%d" (format at 0x3c065e10) with the constants 1, 3, 3 so the text is "1.03 b3" padded with NULs, then a checksum (sum of the bytes after F0, masked with 0x7f) and F7. Sent through fcn.4201a794 on the MIDI object 0x3fcce448 (a3 passed on); a log line is written before and after. The version numbers are immediates in the code. Read in full. The displayed/SysEx tuple 1,3,3 is hard-coded independently of ESP-IDF app metadata string v1.02_b2-232-gdda56c3c-dirty present in the original ELF and UF2. Code does not establish the reason for their difference.

name: MidiSysexController__processMessage
description: Sysex dispatcher (a2 = sysex controller at controller+0x250, a3 = message buffer: u32 length then the message bytes starting with F0, a4 = port (0 USB, 1 DIN by the two call sites in the output task), a5 = 1 from the thunk). Logs "Sysex received with length %d". Drops the message when length < 4, byte 5 is not 0x3E, byte 6 is neither 0x2F nor 0, or the device id in byte 7 is neither global setting 3 nor 0x7F. Logs "MsgId %d" (byte 8); a message with byte 6 = 0 is dropped after that log. Commands by byte 8: 0x10 MidiSysexController__onSoundDump; 0x11 store byte 9 at this+0 and send the current sound (0x3fccf428) with dumpSound; 0x12 preset dump request (slot = byte 10 << 7 | byte 11, log "MSGID_PRESET_DUMP_REQUEST for slot %d"), slot > 0x167 gives sendResponse code 2, else dumpPreset; 0x13 onPresetDump_1; 0x14 preset DELETE request (log "MSGID_PRESET_DELETE_REQUEST for slot %d", same slot format): slot > 0x167 gives response code 2, a free slot gives code 1, otherwise a controller event of kind 17 {0, slot, 17, 0} is put in the ring 0x3fcd3298 and the response is code 0; 0x20 preset names request (start = byte 10 << 7 | byte 11, count = byte 12 << 7 | byte 13, log "MSGID_PRESET_NAMES_REQUEST for slot %d count %d"), count 0 or above 0x168 gives code 6, else sendPresetNames(start, min(0x168 - start, count)); 0x30 dumpScreen; 0x40 version reply (0x4201bab4). Byte 9 of the request is stored at this+0 for 0x11, 0x12, 0x14, 0x20, 0x30 and 0x40 and is echoed by sendResponse. Other commands are ignored. Correction to the older notes: command 0x14 is delete, not select or check.

name: MidiClock__handleSystemMessage
description: Handles MIDI system messages (status a3 >= 0xf0, data a4 and a5, 64-bit timestamp in a6 and a7) on the controller a2. 0xF2 song position: position = (d2 << 7) | d1 stored at +0x224, ticks = position * 6 stored at +0x228, logs "MIDI SongPos beat %d". The messages 0xF8, 0xFA, 0xFB and 0xFC are ignored unless the clock-enable byte at this+0x220 is set (0xFF reset is not gated). 0xFA start: state +0x218 = 2, tick count +0x21c = 0, logs "MIDI Start". 0xFB continue: state 3, count 0, logs "MIDI Continue". 0xFC stop: state 5, logs "MIDI Stop". 0xFF reset: state 5, +0x224 = +0x228 = 0, logs "MIDI Reset". 0xF8 clock tick: the tick position +0x228 is incremented, the timestamp is stored in a ring of 64 8-byte entries at this+8 (index +0x208, count +0x21c incremented). State 0 becomes 1 on the first tick. States 2 and 3 become 4 and the timestamp is stored at +0x210/+0x214 as the reference. In state 4, when the new timestamp is at most 63 units after the previous one, the +0x228 increment is undone. Other states only store the timestamp. States: 0 idle, 1 ticks seen, 2 start, 3 continue, 4 running, 5 stopped (names by use). The timestamp unit is microseconds by the tempo math of MidiClock__fillTransportRecord (inferred, source of the timestamp not read here).

name: MidiClock__fillTransportRecord
description: Fills a transport record a3 from the clock state a2. If the byte at this+0 is 0 the record is the default: tempo 120.0 (double at +8), flag bytes at +0, +1, +16 and +32 cleared, doubles at +24 and +40 zero. Otherwise: byte +0 = 1 when state (+0x218) is 1 to 4; byte +1 = tempo (+0x240) is not below 5.0 (result of a ROM double compare, the exact compare function is assumed); tempo double copied to +8. States 2 to 4: +40 = song position (+0x224) * 0.25 (quarter notes) with byte +32 = 1, and +24 = tick count (+0x21c) / 24 with byte +16 = 1 (also stored at +0x248). State 1: +24 = tick count / 24 with byte +16 = 1. Other states: +16 and +32 cleared. For states 1 and 4 the tempo is re-estimated unless less than 500000 timestamp units have passed since the last estimate: the code walks back through the timestamp ring (up to count - 1 entries) to the first entry at least 500000 older than the newest, then tempo = steps * 2500000 / (newest - entry), which equals BPM for 24 ticks per quarter with microsecond timestamps. A tempo below 5.0 or above 1000.0 is rejected (byte +16 cleared and the old tempo kept; a stored tempo below 5.0 is reset to 120.0 first). The tempo is saved at +0x240 and the state at +0x238. Not confirmed: what sets the byte at this+0.

name: DemoPlayer__start
description: Boot demo player start (a2 = player object inside the controller at controller+0x1af8). Imports the SysEx sound dump of table entry 0 (table 0x3fca04bc, stride 12: pointer, length, base note at +8, step at +9, time byte at +10, note count at +11) with fcn.4201a848 on the controller 0x3fcce448, sets entry index +8 = 0, step counter +1 = 0, current note +0 = entry byte +8, pending flag +2 = 1, and the due time +4 = (uint32)(double(64-bit counter at np+0x38) + 4.0 x double at np+0x28), where np is the note processor from fcn.4201467c (ROM long long to double, multiply, add and convert routines). Fully read. Started by Controller__tick (state byte 1 and the ms time at controller+0x1b04 reached).

name: DemoPlayer__switchEntry
description: Switch to the other demo entry: entry index +8 = (index + 1) mod 2, imports that entry's SysEx dump with fcn.4201a848, sets note +0 from entry byte +8, pending flag +2 = 1, step counter +1 = 0 and the due time +4 as in DemoPlayer__start. Called only from DemoPlayer__tick. Fully read.

name: DemoPlayer__tick
description: Demo player tick (called every Controller__tick while the state byte is 2). Returns while the 64-bit counter at np+0x38 is below the due time at this+4. If the step counter +1 equals the entry's note count (byte +11) it calls DemoPlayer__switchEntry. If the pending flag +2 is set it sends a note-on {0x90, note, 100, zeros} (11-byte message, fifth argument 2) through the MIDI router fcn.42019bdc on 0x3fcce448, clears the flag and adds (entry byte +10 x double at np+0x28 - 1000.0) to the due time. Otherwise it sends the note-off {0x80, note, 100}, increments the step counter; after the last note the due time is increased by 0x15888 (88,200), otherwise the note becomes (note + entry byte +9) with 12 subtracted when above 71, the due time is increased by 1000 and the flag is set. Entry 0: base 60, step 3, byte +10 = 112, 65 notes; entry 1: base 60, step 3, byte +10 = 16, 4 notes. The units of the due time (samples are assumed) and the role of the double at np+0x28 are not established. Fully read.

name: Midi__injectNoteOff
description: Builds an 11-byte message {0x80, note = byte this+0, velocity 100, zeros} and passes it to the MIDI message router fcn.42019bdc on 0x3fcce448 with fifth argument 0 (the demo player passes 2). Called from fcn.4201a19b, inside the controller event handler fcn.4201a0d4 (the listing there is partly desynchronised, so the exact event is not identified). Fully read.

name: UiSender__postQueue58
description: Invoker of the std::function at ui+0x17f0: sends the item pointed to by a3 to the queue at 0x3fccff58 with timeout 0; logs with level 3 (strings 0x3c066a18, 0x3c066a1c) when the send fails.

name: UiSender__postQueue54
description: Invoker of the std::function at ui+0x17e0: sends the item pointed to by a3 to the queue at 0x3fccff54 (the 24-byte engine event queue from the notes) with timeout 0; logs with level 3 (strings 0x3c066a18, 0x3c066a58) when the send fails.

name: UiSender__postQueue60
description: Invoker of the std::function at ui+0x17d0: sends the item pointed to by a3 to the queue whose handle is stored at 0x3fccff60 with a timeout of 200 ticks (fcn.40384af8, queue send shape); if the send fails it logs an error line with level 3 (fcn.4038a91c) using strings at 0x3c066a18 and 0x3c066a94 and the value at a3+8.

name: UITask__body
description: Body of the "UI task" (UI object at 0x3fccff6c). First calls UI__switchToDefaultPage (fcn.4201d11c). Then installs three std::function senders into the UI object, each by moving the old one to the stack and destroying it (fcn.4204ee08): ui+0x17d0 (manager fcn.4204edcc, invoker fcn.4201c538, posts to queue 0x3fccff60), ui+0x17e0 (fcn.4204ede0 / fcn.4201c508, posts to queue 0x3fccff54) and ui+0x17f0 (fcn.4204edf4 / fcn.4201c4d8, posts to queue 0x3fccff58); manager at +8 and invoker at +12 of each object. Then loops forever: (1) while queue 0x3fccff64 has items (fcn.40384fa4), receives one with timeout 0 (fcn.40384d98) into 4 words and calls the central UI event dispatcher fcn.4201d680(ui, w0, w1, w2, w3); (2) while queue 0x3fccff5c has items, receives 3 words and calls UI__broadcastMidi (fcn.4201d4b4); (3) calls fcn.4201d498 (UI service step); (4) delays one tick (fcn.40385e4c(1)). The two queue calls are identified by their argument shapes (queue messages waiting, queue receive), not by symbols.

name: UITask__start
description: UI task start. Calls the FreeRTOS task-create function fcn.4038712c with code = fcn.4201c56c, name = the string "UI task" (0x3c066adc), stack depth 0x1000, task argument 0, priority 1, task-handle output pointer 0x3fccff68 and core 0 (stack argument). Correction: 0x3fccff68 is the handle output, not the task argument (the earlier text said argument). Argument meaning follows the usual create-task signature (inferred from the argument shapes; the IDF function has no symbol in the binary).

name: UserInterface__queuePump
description: Queue pump with three loops. Loop A drains queue 0x3fccff60 (16-byte UI events) into the ring buffer object at 0x3fcd3298 (buffer pointer +4, capacity +8, write index +16, count +20, 16-byte items); when the ring is full it logs "CircularBuffer::write: is full!" (tag ChutneyLog). Loop B drains queue 0x3fccff54 and for each 24-byte item copies it with ROM memcpy and calls Engine__sendEngineEvent(0x3fca3974, event). Loop C drains queue 0x3fccff58 (11-byte items) and sends each to the DIN UART (MidiUart__sendShort with object 0x3fcd1de8) and to USB MIDI (MidiUsb__sendShort with object 0x3fcd2210). Not confirmed: who reads the ring buffer 0x3fcd3298 and who calls the pump.

name: UserInterface__processEvent
description: Posts the 16-byte item {a3,a4,a5,a6} to queue 0x3fccff64 without waiting (xQueueGenericSend, timeout 0). When the queue is full it logs the string "uiEventRxQueue full!" (tag "UI"). Called from the controller handlers (call sites 0x42019892, 0x4201992d, 0x4201a4a1, 0x4201a505, 0x4201a5b3, 0x4201a5d6, 0x4201a78e, 0x4201a819, 0x4201a83b), so queue 0x3fccff64 is filled from the controller side. The consumer is the UI dispatcher 0x4201d680 (earlier rounds).

name: UserInterface__processMidiInput
description: Posts one 11-byte MIDI item (the low 11 bytes of the words a3, a4, a5: three MIDI bytes followed by an 8-byte timestamp) to queue 0x3fccff5c without waiting. When the queue is full it logs "uiMidiMessageRxQueue full!" (tag "UI"). The this argument is not used. Called by the message router 0x42019bdc for every incoming message.

name: UserInterface__createQueues
description: Creates five FreeRTOS queues of 128 entries each with xQueueGenericCreate and stores the handles: 0x3fccff64 (16-byte items, UI event receive queue), 0x3fccff60 (16-byte items, UI events posted by the UI event post 0x4201d010), 0x3fccff5c (11-byte items, incoming MIDI messages), 0x3fccff58 (11-byte items, outgoing short MIDI messages, drained by the pump 0x4201c6c0 to DIN and USB), 0x3fccff54 (24-byte items, engine events).

name: ParamValueOverlay__draw
description: Draws the parameter value overlay (page at ui+0x98c, vtable 0x3c073210). Arguments: this (this+12 = parameter store), a3 = framebuffer, a4 = UI parameter index (limit 0x230), a5 = y offset. Reads the value (fcn.4204f8dc), ParamInfo__isBipolar, ParamInfo__isStepped, formats the value text with fcn.42019024 into a 32-byte buffer, gets the parameter name with fcn.42018c58, draws both strings (fcn.42028e0c, fcn.42028b60, width from fcn.42028ef8; stepped parameters use x positions from the value text width, continuous ones fixed positions) and a bar: a frame 120 x 4 pixels at x = 4, y = offset + 18 (Framebuffer__rectOutline) and a fill (fcn.4204f804) of value x 120 pixels for unipolar, from the centre x = 64 outward for bipolar, and step/(steps-1) for stepped parameters (clamped 0 to 1). Role and bar maths read completely; pixel positions of the text were not decoded.

name: Page__drawFrameAndOverlays
description: Page draw (vt 0x3c073220; a2 = page, a3 = framebuffer). Clears the whole 128 x 64 framebuffer area with fcn.4204f868 and draws a one-pixel outline of the whole screen with fcn.4204f720 (both with the object at framebuffer+0x400 as first argument), then calls ParamValueOverlay__draw (fcn.4201c9c4) twice: with the parameter index s16 at page+16 and y offset 3, and with the index s16 at page+18 and y offset 33. Correction: it clears the full screen, not two regions.

name: UI__ctor
description: Constructor of the global UI object at 0x3fccff6c. Initialises fields and builds the pages in place: colours at ui+8..28; SoundListPage__ctor at ui+0x2c; pages with vtables 0x3c073788 at ui+0xb8 and 0x3c073854 at ui+0xc4; FrontPanel__ctor (fcn.4201e108) at ui+0x198 with the parameter store at ui+0x9a4; Play page 0x3c073688 at ui+0x534; Record page 0x3c0736d0 at ui+0x548; step page 0x3c073758 at ui+0x584; LayerPage__ctor at ui+0x5ac; HeaderPage__ctor at ui+0x75c; settings page 0x3c07380c at ui+0x780; 0x3c0738ec at ui+0x790; DebugPage__ctor at ui+0x7ac; the modal with vtable 0x3c0738c8 at ui+0x878; list helper 0x3c0736ac at ui+0x964; the parameter overlay page 0x3c073210 at ui+0x98c. Calls Sound__resetEditState on the object at ui+0x9a4, clears the 1024-byte display buffer at ui+0x12a8 (the buffer sent by dumpScreen), sets the font descriptors 0x3c073b40 and 0x3c07423c at ui+0x1600+172/176, clears the timer and popup fields (ui+0x1600+180..., ui+0x1700+188 current popup = 0), zeroes the three callback objects at ui+0x17d0, 0x17e0, 0x17f0 and installs the 4-item actions list (strings at 0x3fca04d4) with the select callback fcn.4201d274 at ui+0x978 to ui+0x988. Read completely; the sub-constructors are described separately.

name: ParamOverlay__trigger
description: Decides when the parameter value overlay opens (UI object a2, a3 = s16 value, control pair in this+11 and this+12, a10 time in ms from the microsecond clock divided by 1000). Skips when bit 7 of byte this+11 is set or byte this+13 is non-zero (this function sets +13 = 1 at the start; where it is cleared again was not found). Keeps the current pair {+16 s16 pair, +18 value, +20 time} and moves the previous to +24/+28 when the pair changes. Resets the hold timer +32 and stops if the previous pair is invalid, more than 400 ms old, or had the same value. Otherwise the first call starts the timer, and after more than 199 ms of continued change, and only when the UI is idle (ui+0x900+96 clear, ui+0x1600+188 clear, current popup ui+0x1700+188 null or ui+0x98c or ui+0x3cc), it stores the pair and value at ui+0x900+156, makes the page at ui+0x98c current, sets a 400 ms deadline at ui+0x1600+184 with the active flag ui+0x1600+180 = 1 and the redraw flag ui+0x1200+164. Read completely.

name: UI__sendEvent
description: Sends one UI event (a2 = ui, a3 = event of three words: word 0 parameter id, word 2 event type). For type 6 (parameter write) it first stores the parameter id at ui+0x1290 and calls ParamOverlay__trigger(ui, id). Then, if the std::function at ui+0x17d0 is set (callable at +8, invoker at +12), it calls it with the event pointer. Used by the pot, encoder and step editor code to push parameter changes to the engine side. Read in full.

name: UI__setCurrentPart
description: Stores the part number a3 at ui+0x9a0 (the current part; the per-part parameter index adds part x 0x54) and sends the 24-byte message {type 12, sext7(part), 0, 0, 0, 0} through the std::function at ui+0x17e0. The identification of ui+0x9a0 as the current part is from the pot writer notes (UI parameter index = index + part x 0x54).

name: UI__updateModeLeds
description: Sets the page indicator LEDs from the current page state (ui+0x1298). Writes the shift LED (id 10, board 0x3fcd1b78 + 0x20c) from the shift flag ui+0, and the state words of LEDs 11, 12, 13, 14 (board + 0x21c, 0x22c, 0x23c, 0x24c). State 0: LED 14 = 1; state 1: LED 14 = 2; state 2: LED 12 = 1; states 3, 9, 10: LED 11 = 1; states 4, 5, 6: LED 13 = 1; state 11: all four off; states 7 and 8: no change. All other LEDs of the group are set to 0 in each case. What LED value 2 does (blink or dim) was not read here. Read in full.

name: UI__switchToDefaultPage
description: Page switch to the default page. Sets the dirty byte ui+0x12a4 to 1 and clears byte ui+0x960. If the current page ui+0x24 is the page object at ui+0x7ac it returns. Otherwise it copies the word ui+0x1298 to ui+0x129c (previous state), clears ui+0x1298, makes the default page object at ui+0x2c current, sets byte ui+0x28 to 1, and (when the old page differs from the new one) calls the old page's virtual slot +24 (leave) and then the new page's virtual slot +20 (enter); finally calls fcn.4201d070(ui). Fully traced.

name: UI__setPage
description: Switches the active page (a2 = ui, a3 = state). Always clears the global menu flag ui+0x960 and sets the redraw flag ui+0x12a4. Stores the previous state at ui+0x129c and the new one at ui+0x1298. Page object for the state, stored at ui+0x24: 0 ui+0x2c, 1 ui+0xb8, 2 ui+0x198 (front panel), 3 ui+0x780 (settings), 4 ui+0x534 (play), 5 ui+0x548 (record), 6 ui+0x584 (step editor), 7 ui+0x5ac (sound list / layers), 8 ui+0x75c (multi/single), 9 ui+0x790 (info), 10 ui+0x79c (mappings), 11 ui+0x7ac (debug view); any other state sets no page. While the debug page ui+0x7ac is active only state 3 is accepted (it returns to ui+0x780). If the page changed, the byte ui+0x28 is set to 1, slot +24 (leave) of the old page and slot +20 (enter) of the new page are called, and UI__updateModeLeds runs. Read in full. [Stage 16: also called by CustomADSR__showPage.]

name: UI__globalMenuSelect
description: Selection callback of the global popup menu (a2 = closure with the ui at word 0, a3 = selection record, word 0 = index). Clears ui+0x960 and sets the redraw flag. Index 0 (Info): UI__setPage(9). Index 1 (Map CC): clears ui+0x16bc, sets the overlay object ui+0x17bc to ui+0x79c (via the mappings page object), sets the flag ui+0x16b4 and the deadline ui+0x16b8 = now_ms + 1,200,000 (timer arithmetic as in UI__showText). Index 2 (Mappings): UI__setPage(10). Index 3 (Close): nothing. Read in full.

name: UI__showText
description: Shows a timed text message (a2 = ui, a3 = text pointer, a4 = duration in ms). Clears byte ui+0x960, copies 256 bytes from a3 to the message buffer ui+0x16bc (ROM memcpy), clears the overlay word ui+0x17bc, sets the deadline ui+0x16b8 = t + a4 and the active byte ui+0x16b4 = 1, and sets the dirty byte. Used for "Saved", "Copied!", "Pasted!", "Initialized!", "Empty" (all 2000 ms in the callers read). [Stage 16: also shows LATCH ON / LATCH OFF (1500 ms).]

name: UI__setOverlay
description: Sets the modal overlay object (a2 = ui, a3 = object pointer or 0, a4 = duration in ms). Clears byte ui+0x960 and the first byte of the message text buffer ui+0x16bc, stores a3 in the word ui+0x17bc; when a3 is non-zero sets the deadline ui+0x16b8 = t + a4 (t = fcn.4037a37c / 1000) and the active byte ui+0x16b4 = 1, otherwise clears the active byte (removes the overlay). Always sets the dirty byte ui+0x12a4. The overlay object is drawn through its virtual slot +16 by UI__drawInfoPopup.

name: UI__drawInfoPopup
description: Popup draw (a2 = ui). If the first byte of the message buffer ui+0x16bc is non-zero: clears and outlines the rectangle x 6, y 12, w 110, h 40 (fcn.4204f868, fcn.4204f720, drawing object ui+0x16a8), draws the message text with fcn.42028b60 at x 14, y 24, width 108 (the text pointer ui+0x16bc is the stack argument, ui+0x16a9 and ui+0x16ac are other arguments), then sets the dirty byte ui+0x12a4. If the message is empty and the overlay word ui+0x17bc is a non-zero object pointer, it calls that object's virtual slot +16 with the framebuffer and sets the dirty byte. Corrections to earlier text: the byte at ui+0x16bc is the start of the 256-byte message text, and the slot +16 call goes to the overlay object, not the current page.

name: UI__tick
description: UI redraw tick (a2 = ui). Time t = fcn.4037a37c divided by 1000 (ROM 64-bit divide 0x4000225c). Redraws only when (dirty byte ui+0x12a4 is set or more than 1000 ms passed since the stamp at ui+0x12a0) and more than 50 ms passed since that stamp. A redraw stores t in the stamp, clears the dirty byte, clears the 1,024-byte framebuffer at ui+0x12a8 (memset 0), calls the current page's virtual slot +12 (draw) with the framebuffer, then the popup logic: when the active byte ui+0x16b4 is set and either the first byte of the message buffer ui+0x16bc or the overlay word ui+0x17bc is non-zero it calls UI__drawInfoPopup; when the deadline word ui+0x16b8 is below t it clears the active byte, the message first byte and the overlay word. Then it draws the generic 3-row list overlay fcn.42022120 at ui+0x964 when byte ui+0x960 is set, and finally calls the display transfer fcn.420273f0(0x3fcd1de4, framebuffer).

name: UI__serviceStep
description: Per-loop step of the UI task. If byte this+54 is set calls UI__tick; then calls fcn.42025074(this+0x17c0, this) every loop. Correction: fcn.42025074 is not a wavetable cache constructor; it is a once-per-second debug console and statistics report (see its entry).

name: UI__broadcastMidi
description: MIDI input fan-out in the UI task (a2 = ui, a3 to a5 = the three MIDI bytes). Calls fcn.42022bc0 on ui+0x548 (Play/arp page note-on handler), fcn.4204f0f8 on ui+0x584 (a no-op method) and fcn.4201dee4 on ui+0x79c (Map CC learn hook) with the three bytes, then, when the log byte ui+0x17cc is set, writes the three bytes to the log at level 3 (fcn.4038a91c, tag string 0x3c0642d8, format 0x3c066b94, timestamp from fcn.4038a9a8).

name: UI__onButton
description: Button handler (a2 = ui, a3 = button id, a4 = pressed). ids 0 to 3: pressed opens the sound list (state 7). id 4: pressed opens the multi/single page (state 8). id 5 (Shift, flag ui+0, raw state ui+1): a press toggles the latched shift flag and clears ui+2 and stores the time in ui+4; a release keeps shift latched only when no other button was used meanwhile (ui+2 = 0) and the press was shorter than 400 ms, otherwise shift is cleared; then UI__updateModeLeds. id 6: with shift opens the global menu (ui+0x960 = 1), else state 3 (settings). id 7: with shift runs the init-sound confirm (fcn.42021b0c on ui+0x2c), else state 2 (front panel). id 8: with shift state 5 (record); without shift, and only when the byte at 0x3fccf425 is not 1 or 2 (probably the ArpSeqMode mirror; unconfirmed), a press opens state 4 (play page) and calls fcn.4202202c, a release returns to the previous state (ui+0x129c) and calls PlayPage__noteOff. id 9: with shift runs fcn.42023274 on ui+0xb8 and opens state 1, else state 0. Other ids are ignored. Release events of the page buttons do nothing. Read in full. [Stage 16: called by Latch__uiButtonHook for every event except button 15 press.]

name: UI__dispatchEvent
description: Central UI event dispatcher (a2 = ui, a3 = control id, a4 = value, a5 = event type, a6 = extra pointer or value). Types: 0 button, 2 pot, 3 encoder, 5 info text, 7 parameter update from the engine, 12 and 13 page-change marker. Bookkeeping: for types 2 and 3 the pair (type ui+8, id ui+9) is compared with the previous event; a repeat of the same control without a page change increments the saturating counter ui+10, otherwise the counter restarts at 0 and the control pair is stored in ui+11 and ui+12 (ui+13 = 0); other types clear the pair to 0xFF. Routing: if the global menu is open (ui+0x960) the event goes to the menu list handler ListSelector__onInput at ui+0x964. Otherwise an active modal overlay (ui+0x17bc, enabled by ui+0x16b4) gets it first (overlay slot +8); only the overlays at ui+0x3cc and ui+0x98c let the event continue to the pages. Then all 13 page handlers are called in this order, each with an is-current-page flag, the repeat counter and the page-changed byte: ui+0x2c, ui+0xb8, front panel ui+0x198, ui+0x534, ui+0x548, ui+0x584, ui+0x5ac, ui+0x75c, ui+0x780, ui+0x790, ui+0x79c, ui+0x7ac (the popup list at ui+0x2c and ui+0xb8 use fcn.42021c8c and fcn.4202345c). After routing: type 0 calls UI__onButton and marks ui+2 for any button other than id 5; types 2 and 3 record the control for shift; type 5 logs "Event::UI_INFO_MSG", and for a non-zero id clears ui+0x960, copies 256 bytes of text from the extra pointer to ui+0x16bc, clears the overlay and sets the 10 minute info deadline (now_ms + 600,000) and ui+0x16b4; with id 0 it writes the extra value into ui+0x960, ui+0x16bc and ui+0x16b4 (hide); type 7 stores float(value) x 1e-6 at ui+0x9a4 under parameter id a3 (ParamStore__set) and sets the redraw flag; types 12 and 13 set ui+0x28. The repeat control pair is reset to 0xFF at the end. Read in full; the exact meaning of types 12 and 13 is only inferred. [Stage 16: front panel call 0x4201d7fd -> 0x420539f8; UI__onButton call 0x4201d96f -> 0x420538c0; ui+40 store at 0x4201d98f -> CustomADSR__selectHook 0x42054400.]

name: CcMap__nextMapped
description: Finds the next mapped entry in the 120-entry s16 table at 0x3fcce448+12+2*(0x630+n): if this+12 is already 0..119 and its entry is not -1 it keeps it; otherwise searches forward with wrap-around (n modulo 120, using the 0x88888889 reciprocal) for the first entry != -1 and stores that n, or -1 when there is none, in this+12.

name: CcMapPage__draw
description: Draw method of the "CC Mappings" list (a2 = page, a3 = draw context). Calls BlinkPhase__tick, draws the title "CC Mappings" and a line under it. If the selected CC (page+12) is -1 it searches forward from -1 over the 120 CC slots (0 to 119) of the s16 map in the MIDI object (0x3fcce448, table at +0xc60 + 12) for the first mapped one and selects it, or shows "Nothting Mapped" (typo in the firmware) when none is mapped. Otherwise it prints the CC number with "%d", the mapped parameter ("%c: %s" with layer letter and name, or the global name) and the button " Delete "; an unmapped selected CC shows "Not Mapped". Read in full.

name: CcMapPage__askDelete
description: Opens the "Delete Mapping" confirm dialog for the selected CC (page+12; nothing when it is -1): formats "For CC %d" into a local buffer, then calls ValueEditModal__showMode0 on the dialog object at ui+0x878 with the texts "Delete" and "Cancel", the title "Delete Mapping" and the closure CcMapPage__deleteConfirm (page pointer captured, std::function manager 0x4204ef8c). Afterwards it calls the manager once with operation 3 to destroy its local copy of the std::function. Read in full.

name: CcMapPage__onInput
description: Input handler of the Mappings page (ui+0x79c; a3 = control id, a4 = value, a5 = event kind, a7 = pressed). Kind 0, id 10 (Select encoder button): if this page is the active overlay (the Map CC wait state) a press cancels it with UI__setOverlay(ui, 0, 400); otherwise a press opens CcMapPage__askDelete. Kind 3 (encoder 0): moves the selection page+12 up or down through the mapped CC slots among the 120 (0 to 119), skipping unmapped ones and wrapping, by |value| steps; any change sets the redraw flag. Read in full.

name: CcLearnPage__onMidi

When this page is the active overlay and the message is a control change (status 0xB0 to 0xBF) with a CC number up to 119, assigns that CC to the parameter in ui+0x1290 with CcMap__assign on the MIDI object, builds "%d -> %s" with the CC number and ParamInfo__name and shows it for 3000 ms with UI__showText. Read in full.
