name: Allpass2__setCoeffs
description: Second-order all-pass coefficient helper (a2 = coefficient block, a3 = float normalised frequency f, a4 = float pole radius r). Computes c = cos(2 pi f) (libm cosf wrapper 0x4203da08) and stores +4 = 2 r c, +8 = -r^2, +0xc = r^2, +0x10 = -2 r c, +0x14 = 1.0. This is the all-pass H(z) = (r^2 - 2 r c z^-1 + z^-2) / (1 - 2 r c z^-1 + r^2 z^-2). Called by Phaser__process for the first section of each channel (blocks at phaser +0x40 left and +0x2c0 right).

name: EQ__lowShelf
description: Low-shelf coefficient builder (a2 = filter object, a3 = float normalised frequency, a4 = float gain in dB). Gain exactly 0 gives pass-through (b0 = 1.0, others 0, and the object's virtual slot +8 is called to clear its state). Otherwise K = tan(pi f) (libm tanf wrapper 0x4203db98), V = Db__toLinear(|gain|), uses sqrt(2) (3fb504f3) and sqrt(2V) (0x4203d928 sqrtf) with K^2 and V K^2 terms in the Zoelzer shelving form, one set for boost and one for cut, each divided by the common denominator; results are stored at +4 / +8 (feedback), +0xc / +0x10 / +0x14 (b0, b1, b2). The term-by-term formula is not re-derived (unconfirmed).

name: EQ__highShelf
description: High-shelf coefficient builder; same argument list and structure as EQ__lowShelf (a2 = filter object, a3 = normalised frequency, a4 = gain in dB; gain 0 gives pass-through) with the high-shelf form of the Zoelzer coefficients. Term-by-term formula not re-derived (unconfirmed).

name: EQ__peaking
description: Peaking-filter coefficient builder (a2 = filter object, a3 = normalised frequency, a4 = gain in dB, a5 = Q). Gain exactly 0 gives pass-through. Otherwise K = tan(pi f), V = Db__toLinear(|gain|), q = K / Q; with den = 1 + q + K^2, den2 = 1 - q + K^2, numB = 1 + V q + K^2, numC = 1 - V q + K^2, c = 2 (K^2 - 1): for a boost the stored values are b0 = numB / den, b1 = c / den, b2 = numC / den, feedback +4 = -c / den and +8 = -den2 / den; for a cut b0 = den / numB, b1 = c / numB, b2 = den2 / numB, feedback +4 = -c / numB and +8 = -numC / numB. This is the Zoelzer parametric peak filter. Coefficient layout in the filter object: +4 and +8 feedback, +0xc b0, +0x10 b1, +0x14 b2, states from +0x18.
deleting destructor: operator delete(this, 0x3f4); class size 0x3f4, trivial member destruction

name: ReverbCore__setParam
description: Reverb core parameter setter (a2 = core, a3 = index, a4 = float x). Index 8 and above: return. Otherwise x is stored at this+0x3d0+4*idx, then: 0: this+0x1c = x*0.5. 1: v = 16370*x*(1+x) truncated to int, min with 0x7fe0, masked to a multiple of 16 (bits 4 to 14), plus u16 at +8 plus 16, stored as u16 at +10. 2: clamp to 0..1 (NaN gives 0), stored at +0x24. 3: only the raw store. 4: s = 2x-1, then A, B, C are computed and written to this+0x3c4/0x3c8/0x3cc and to every tap record (count at +0x200, records stride 16 from this+0x208, fields +0 A, +4 B, +8 C); if s <= 0: s clamped to -1, A = -0.99 - 1.89*s, B = C = (1-A)*0.5; if s > 0: t = min(0.3*s*s, 1), A = 0.99 - 1.69*t, B = (A+1)*0.5, C = -B. 5: for each of the 36-byte records (count at +0x16c) float at this+0x188+36k = float at this+0x180+36k * 20*x^3. 6: same loop with float at this+0x17c+36k = float at this+0x174+36k * 5*x. 7: this+0x14 = 2x, this+0x10 = 2-2x. Meaning of the fields (diffusion, size, decay and so on) is not confirmed. Corrects the Round 48 text (case 1 is not a plain multiply, case 5 is a cube, case 7 stores 2x).

name: ReverbCore__diffuse
description: Reverb diffuser on a shared 65536-float circular buffer (a2 = diffuser subobject at core+0x28, a3 = buffer, a4 = current write index, a5 = float coefficient from core+0x20, not an audio sample). Fully traced. First applies count at subobject+0x0 of 16-byte all-pass records from +0x4: if i=(write-uint16(record+4)) mod 65536 and j=(i+uint16(record+4)-uint16(record+0)) mod 65536, old values x=buffer[i] and y=buffer[j] yield buffer[i]=coef8*y+coef12*x and buffer[j]=y-coef8*x, for each of 16 samples. Next runs count at +0x144 of 36-byte modulated delay records starting +0x15c: smooth float rate at record+0 toward +4 by 0.01 per block; advance wrapped phase at +8 by 16*rate/44100; triangle=2*phase below 0.5 else 2-2*phase; smooth depth at record-12 toward record-8 by 0.01, multiply by triangle and split integer and fractional parts, then linearly interpolate between adjacent ring samples to write a relocated 16-sample span. Next, count at +0x1d8 of 16-byte records from +0x1dc updates 16 samples by coefficient0*previous + (coefficient4*a5)*current + (coefficient8*a5)*next. Finally count at +0x21c of 12-byte records from +0x220 writes the sum of a ring sample and a5 times another ring sample to a third delayed position, all indices modulo 65536. Buffer operations and coefficient arithmetic verified; no measured spectral response asserted.

name: Reverb__setBuffer
description: Stores the buffer a3 at this+4 and clears 0x40040 bytes (262,208) of it. Only caller is Reverb__attachBuffer (this = part+0xfd0+12).

name: ReverbCore__updateTapGains
description: Computes early-reflection gain entries from float g at core+0x18 and float v at core+0x20. For v > 0.5, use g1=g2=g3=g; otherwise u=2*v, g1=g*(5-4*u), g2=u*g1 and g3=u*g2. Stores g1,g2,-g2,g3,-g3,-g3,-g3 to both seven-tap groups at offsets +0x284,+0x28c,+0x294,+0x29c,+0x2a4,+0x2ac,+0x2b4 and +0x324,+0x32c,+0x334,+0x33c,+0x344,+0x34c,+0x354. No musical labels are asserted for g and v; arithmetic, branch and every write checked against the firmware.

name: ReverbCore__init
description: ReverbCore__init is a straight-line initializer with no runtime control branch. Installs dispatch pointer 0x3c078bd8 at core+0, zeroes ring pointer +4, and stores packed u16 ring indices (0,16) as word 0x00100000 at +8. Current and target gain/feedback floats at +0x18..+0x24 start at 0.5; writes eight 16-byte all-pass records (count +0x28=8), two 36-byte modulated delay records (count +0x16c=2), two 16-byte diffuser three-tap records (count +0x200=2), and two 12-byte delayed-sum records (count +0x244=2), with the literal delay offsets, phase/rate defaults and coefficients. Populates two seven-entry output early-tap arrays with fixed unsigned delay offsets (counts +0x278/+0x27c), then calls ReverbCore__updateTapGains 0x4202ace0. Initializes three-point ring filter position +0x3c0 and coefficients +0x3c4/+0x3c8/+0x3cc, clears field +0x3e0 and ring-clear counter +0x3f0. Every stored constant and destination was traced. Reasons for the designers' exact delay constants, role of +0x3e0 outside this initializer and measured acoustic response are not inferred.

name: ReverbCore__setPreDelay
description: Pre-delay length (a2 = core object, a3 = float PreDelay 0..1): n = trunc(16370 * x + 16370 * x * x) limited to 32736 and rounded down to a multiple of 16 (bits 4..14), and the read position s16 at +10 = (s16 write index at +8) + 16 + n. So the maximum pre-delay is 32,720 samples (about 0.74 s at 44.1 kHz) in steps of 16 samples.

name: ReverbCore__mixTaps
description: Output stage of the reverb core (a2 = core object, a3 = left output block, a4 = right output block, 16 floats each). First copies seven 16-byte groups from the start of the shared buffer (pointer at +4) to the same positions plus 0x40000 bytes (a guard copy so a read that runs past the end of the 65,536-float ring stays valid), then, for each of the +0x278 taps in the table at +0x280 ({16-bit delay, float gain} pairs) adds gain * buffer[(write index - delay + i) mod 65536] to the left output, and likewise for the +0x27c taps at +0x320 into the right output.

name: ReverbCore__process
description: Processes a 16-sample stereo block (a2 core, a3/a4 input L/R, a5/a6 output L/R). If clear counter +0x3f0 is positive, multiply current gains +0x20 and +0x18 by 0.92, recalculate seven tap gains, zero the 16-float block at current pre-delay index +0xa and an additional region tracked by uint16 counter +0xc, decrement +0x3f0, copy input channels to distinct output buffers and then call ReverbCore__mixTaps; no diffuser is run on this branch. Normal path: move current +0x20 toward target +0x24 and current +0x18 toward target +0x1c, using 0.01 of the difference when absolute delta > 0.01, otherwise snap; update tap gains when +0x18 changes. Write the 16 samplewise sums inputL+inputR into the ring at uint16 index core+0xa. If core+0x18 >= 0.45, scale the dry outputs by max(0, 10-20*core+0x18); otherwise copy dry inputs to outputs when pointers differ. Apply a 3-tap filter in place to 16 ring samples using coefficients +0x3c4/+0x3c8/+0x3cc and offset +0x3c0. Call ReverbCore__diffuse with the diffuser subobject core+0x28, ring pointer core+4, uint16 index core+8 and float coefficient core+0x20, then ReverbCore__mixTaps. On both paths increment the uint16 indices at core+8 and core+10 by 16. All branch, arithmetic and call paths read; no physical sound-response claim.

name: Tables__buildSineAndDb
description: Builds two 1024-entry float tables at boot: the sine table at 0x3fcd45d8 (entry 0 = 0, entry k = sin(2 pi k / 1024)) and the dB table at 0x3fcd55d8 (entry i = powf(10, (-200 + 300 * i / 1024) / 20)). Stores the two table pointers in the object 0x3fcd65d8 at +0 and +8 (8-byte entries: pointer and length). The lengths at +4 and +12 are set to 0x400 by the small function at 0x4202b59c.
vt 0x3c082e4c: sets fields +4 and +12 of global 0x3fcd65d8 to 0x400

name: WavetableCache__fillGaps
description: Fills the empty (flag 0) waves of one table by averaging (a2 = cache, a3 = table; recursive, one wave per pass). Returns at once if the flag of wave 0 is 0 (table empty). Scans the flags of waves 1..60; if all are set it returns. Otherwise takes the first empty wave g with the filled wave p = g - 1 before it and looks for the next filled wave n after g; if n exists (up to index 60) the wave at index (p + n) / 2 is set to the byte-wise (unsigned bytes, sum >> 1) average of waves p and n and its flag set; if no later wave is filled the wave at (g + 60) / 2 (the middle between p and a virtual wave 61) is set to the average of wave p and wave 0 of table 88, its flag set. Then it calls itself again. Read in full.

name: WavetableCache__buildTable
description: Copies one table into the cache from a list of 61 wave numbers (a2 = cache, a3 = table number). Wave number list: for tables 0x20..0x37 the RAM list at cache + 0x5627a + (t - 32) x 122; for tables 0x1c..0x4b and 0x58 no list is set up (not valid to call, a null pointer would be read; the dispatcher never does); for all others the ROM list at 0x3c07e240 + 122 x i, where i = t for t up to 75 and t - 48 above 75 (40 lists: tables 0..27 and 76..87). For each of the 61 entries v (u16): 0xffff = write 64 zero bytes and flag 0; v in 246..367 = copy 64 bytes from the user wave pool at cache + 0x56e02 + (v - 246) x 64, flag 1; v below 246 = copy from the ROM wave bank 0x3c079740 + v x 64; v in 368..421 = ROM wave bank wave v - 122 (246..299); any other v = ROM wave 101. Each copy goes to cache + 4 + t x 3904 + 64 w and sets the flag byte at cache + 0x54d44 + 61 t + w to 1. Ends with WavetableCache__fillGaps for the same table. Read in full. For 24 user tables of 61 u16 entries each, the user map occupies cache offsets [0x5627a,0x56dea), leaving the following 24 bytes [0x56dea,0x56e02) outside the valid map. The separate user wave pool begins at +0x56e02. This address boundary by itself does not establish the purpose of the zeroed 24-byte field.

name: WavetableCache__buildSpecialTable88
description: Writes table 88 (cache+0x53e04, 64-byte blocks): block 0 = byte 0x82, then 31 steps of +3 (133 up to 223), the last value repeated once, then 31 steps of -3 (220 down to 130) - a low-amplitude triangle around 128; block 1 = 64 bytes of 0xC0; block 2 = 0xC0 then 63 descending values 191 down to 129. Then sets all 61 key-flag bytes of table 88 (cache+0x5623c = 0x54d44 + 88 x 61) to 1. Arguments: the cache object only. Checked against the disassembly and the table-base formula.

name: WavetableCache__smoothBlock
description: Smoothing step (cache a2, table a3, source slot a4, destination slot a5). Block address = cache + 4 + (table * 61 + slot) * 64; samples are bytes. Copies the 64 source bytes to the stack, adds a boundary byte on each side (the bitwise inverse of the first and of the last source byte), and writes destination[i] = (src[i-1] + 6 * src[i] + src[i+1] + 4) >> 3, that is a (1, 6, 1) / 8 low-pass with rounding. Then sets the destination key flag at cache + 0x54d44 + table * 61 + slot to 1. Read from the code (addx2 chain at 0x4202b8f2-0x4202b908).

name: WavetableCache__buildKarplusStrongTable
description: Builds one Karplus-Strong style table: block 0 and block 60 are filled with 0 or 255 from a 16-bit LFSR (state at cache+2, feedback mask 0xffff8125), then 23 passes of fcn.4202b884 smooth block i into i+1 for destinations 1 to 23 and block 61-i into 60-i for destinations 59 down to 37. Key blocks are therefore 0-23 and 37-60; blocks 24-36 stay unflagged (interpolated at build time, inference). Called for table 71 (seed 74, name 'K+St. #1'), table 72 (seed 0x5678, 'K+St. #2') and table 73 (seed 113, 'K+St. #3'); the seed is written to cache+2 before the call.

name: WavetableCache__buildFromRecords
description: Builds one table from 61 records of 8 bytes (a2 = cache, a3 = table number, a4 = record pointer; used for table 74 with records 0x3fca08f4 and table 75 with 0x3fca070c). Copies the 17-byte amplitude table from 0x3c078bf8 to the stack. Per record r (wave r): fills the 64 wave bytes with 0x80, then for each of three partial pairs (b0,b1), (b2,b3), (b4,b5): if b0 is below 8 it adds, to samples 0 to 22 only, the value sine[phase] >> b0 (sign-symmetric shift) where the sine is the 184-entry signed byte table at 0x3c078c4c, the phase starts at b1/2 and advances by b1 per sample, wrapping by +72 (mod 256) when above 183. Then samples 33 to 63 are set to the negation of samples 30 down to 0 (antisymmetric half cycle; samples 23 to 32 stay 0x80 unless noise is added). Noise part when byte 6 is non-zero: amp = amplitude table[b6 & 15], length = (b7 & 31) + 6; the shift-register state at cache+0 is set to 0xFFD5, then for all 64 samples the current offset is subtracted from the sample (initial offset -(b6 & 15)), a counter adds length each sample and when it exceeds 12 it drops by 23 and the state steps (shift left, xor 43 when bit 14 of the old state is set) choosing the new offset as +amp or -amp. State is 0xFFFF after each record. No flag bytes are written here: the interpolation routine fcn.4202b5ac skips a table whose wave 0 flag is clear, which is the case for tables 74 and 75, and all 61 waves are built directly. Whole function read.

name: WavetableCache__buildSynthTables
description: Switch on the table number (a3 & 0xff) over the 24 code-built tables 28-31 and 56-75 (names from the array at 0x3fca05ac); a2 = cache. Table t starts at cache + 4 + t*3904 (wave w at + w*64), its 61 flags at cache + 0x54d44 + t*61. 28 MW Sync: 6-bit sawtooth, rising frequency. 29 MicroPWM: shrinking positive pulse. 30 Glassy: waves 0 and 60 only (half-sine from 0x3c078f00 and its 2-bit version), rest interpolated. 31 SquareHP: key waves 0, 30, 60. Wave 60 = 0x80 up to sample 48, then 0x81,0x81,0x83,0x83,0x87,0x87,0x8F,0x8F,0x9F,0x9F,0xBF,0xBF,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF (samples 49 to 63); wave 30 = 0xC0 - j (0xC0 down to 0x81); wave 0 = 0xFF - (wave60 & 0x7F). 56-58 SawSync, 59-61 PulSync, 62-64 SinSync (sine from the 1024-entry s16 table at 0x3c078f40): phase-accumulator sweeps with the last 16 samples faded to the centre. 65 PWMPulse, 66 PWM Saw: pulse and bent-ramp morphs. 67 FuzzWave: low-passed sliding window of ROM bytes at 0x3c078e00. 68 Distortd: splice of ROM blocks 0x3c078d04 and 0x3c078e80. 69 HeavyFuz: wave 0 = byte 1 then 63 values of 0x01/0xFF from a 16-bit LFSR (seed 200, shift left, xor 43 and toggle the value when bit 15 shifts out; state kept at cache+0); each later wave = previous wave bytes 1-63 moved to 0-62 plus one new last byte (the previous last byte, toggled when the LFSR fires); all 61 waves flagged. 70 FuzzSync: wave 0 = 64 bytes copied from 0x3c078c0c; wave w (1-60) is a pattern repeated every 124-2w bytes (starts at every multiple of the period up to byte 63): byte 0 = 72, then src[1..61-w] from 0x3c078ec0, then the complement (NOT) of src[61-w] down to src[0]; later waves overwrite the spill of earlier ones so all 64 bytes of each wave are written; waves 1-60 flagged. 71-73 call fcn.4202b928 (Karplus-Strong seeds 74, 0x5678, 113 stored at cache+2), 74 and 75 call fcn.4202b9f4 with records 0x3fca08f4 and 0x3fca070c. Whole function read from aligned disassembly; not run. Unconfirmed: whether the wave 0 flag of table 70 is set anywhere (this code sets only waves 1-60), and the return value of the ROM copy at 0x400011f4 is assumed to be the destination. Cross-function header resolution (Round 104): HeavyFuz stores the feedback state at cache+0 with s16i at 0x4202c3c2 and 0x4202c3f9, then reads it with l16ui at 0x4202c41a for subsequent waves. This proves cache+0 is working LFSR state, not necessarily a format or version field. Cache__init initially writes 100, but the HeavyFuz builder starts from local 200 before its first identified feedback-state read. Round 105: The HeavyFuz branch ignores init literal 100 as an LFSR seed; it derives the first stored feedback value from local seed 200 at 0x4202c39a and stores that state at cache+0 before the identified l16ui read. This is about the generator path, not evidence of the original author intent.

name: WavetableCache__buildAll
description: Builds all 89 tables of the cache (a2 = cache base). Loop over table t = 0..88, dispatch: t in 0x20..0x37 (user tables 32..55): no builder, only WavetableCache__fillGaps; t in 0x1c..0x4b not in the user range (28..31 and 56..75): WavetableCache__buildSynthTables (0x4202bb70) then fillGaps; t = 88: WavetableCache__buildSpecialTable88 (0x4202b7f0) then fillGaps, then return; all other tables (0..27 and 76..87): WavetableCache__buildTable (ROM definitions) then fillGaps. Because the user tables have no builder and their map is zero at init, the first flag of each stays 0 and fillGaps returns at once, so tables 32..55 stay all zero bytes. Read in full.

name: MidiPort__isReady

name: Format__snprintf

Obtains the current errno pointer, rejects a negative size by setting errno to 139 and returning -1, sets up a local string-output stream with at most size-1 writable characters (or zero when size is zero), and invokes the internal format engine at 0x42041c00. If the format engine returns less than -1 it sets errno to 139; if size is nonzero it NUL-terminates the current output position. Returns the internal formatting result otherwise. Used to print both formatted parameter values and boot version text.
